Salt Lake City east and west

Utah's capital anchors the valley from its northeast corner, covering 110.8 square miles with the Wasatch Range at its back, the Oquirrh Mountains across the way and the Great Salt Lake to the northwest. The Jordan River crosses the city, average elevation is 4,327 feet, and the 2020 census found 199,723 residents.

Neighborhoods on the east side, such as the Avenues, 9th and 9th, Yalecrest, Federal Heights and Sugar House, lean more affluent. Poplar Grove, Rose Park and Glendale on the west side lean more working-class and diverse. Yalecrest and Rose Park are different worlds, so think about which side yours is on before settling on a price.

Older housing and the Avenues

Brigham Young led Latter-day Saint pioneers here in 1847. The place was incorporated in 1851, platted in 1857 and named Great Salt Lake City until 1868, when Great was dropped. Rail arrived in 1870, and statehood in 1896 made it the capital.

Many Victorian-era homes stand in the Avenues, a historic district. Older houses cost more to maintain, and an owner facing a long repair list may find a cash sale simpler.

The Wasatch Fault and your house

Along the mountain front, the Wasatch Fault has a Salt Lake City segment beneath the city, which last broke roughly 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years are put at 57 percent, and the ground could shift by as much as 20 feet at the surface. Buildings across the valley took damage when a magnitude 5.7 quake struck near Magna on March 18, 2020.

  • At least 42 percent of Wasatch Front buildings are at risk of moderate to severe damage in a strong quake.
  • Liquefaction is a risk where buildings sit on soft lake sediments.
  • Gas, electric and water lines are expected to be damaged after a large quake.

Quake risk is no barrier to selling. When a house shows damage from the 2020 quake or from settling, selling as-is is often easier than repairing first.

Winters and what they do to a roof

The seasons swing hard, from cold winters to hot summers. At the airport, precipitation averages about 15.5 inches and snowfall roughly 52 inches, with about 127 days at or below freezing. Mean daily highs are 38.6 degrees in January and 94.0 degrees in July.

The freeze count is what matters for a house. Roofs, gutters, sprinkler lines and exposed pipes endure repeated freezing and thawing, which makes buyers wary of deferred roof or plumbing work.

Rental business license

Each residential rental in the city needs its own current business license. Single and double family homes and similar rentals fall under the Landlord/Tenant Initiative, known as the Good Landlord Program. Joining can cut per-unit fees by up to 95 percent. The ordinance began on September 1, 2011.

Heirs of a former rental and owners weary of managing a duplex run into this. Tenants can stay through a cash purchase, and it is fine to ask us how that touches the lease and your license.

Short-term rental rules

Nightly rentals need a city business license and are limited to approved zoning districts. One person may hold just one short-term rental license in the city.

  • A license covers one property and one dwelling unit.
  • The minimum stay is two consecutive nights.
  • A unit may be rented for no more than 200 nights per calendar year.
  • In a building with more than 11 units, up to 10 percent may be covered.
  • Condominium units need an HOA authorization letter.

MU2, MU3, D1 and GMU are among the approved districts. Look up your address's zoning before promising a buyer short-term rental income, and call Business Licensing at (801) 535-7980 for fees and dates.

Property tax dates and penalties

City homes are billed by the county. Valuation date is January 1. If you live in the home, 45 percent of the value of the buildings and up to one acre of land is exempt.

Tax stepDate or amount
Valuation notice goes outLate July
Window to appeal at the Board of EqualizationAugust 1 to September 15, or 45 days after the notice if that is later
Tax bills in the mailBy November 1
Taxes dueNovember 30
Penalty once delinquent (December 1)Greater of 2.5 percent or $10
Reduced penalty if paid by January 31Greater of 1 percent or $10
Treasurer certifies delinquent taxesMarch 15

Tax sales usually happen on the fourth Thursday of May.

How to appeal your valuation

File form BE01 with evidence of what the house is worth. A late appeal can be taken up to March 31 of the following year, though only for narrow reasons, so file on time.

Selling with taxes owed

Back taxes will not stop a sale. Delinquent taxes are certified each March 15 and head toward the May tax sale, so waiting only makes the situation harder. The title company pulls the balance with penalties and pays it out of your proceeds at closing. For a payoff figure ahead of time, ask the county Treasurer.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What a seller should disclose

The standard Utah purchase contract has sellers disclose known problems, typically on a Seller's Property Condition Disclosure form. Your title or escrow company can say which forms fit your sale. Topics include roof leaks, flooding and drainage, mold, structural or soil problems, permits and HOA details.

Even heirs who never lived there should report what they know, and a Utah real estate attorney can answer doubts. You can look up property records at the county Recorder, 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Listing, selling yourself or selling for cash

Owners here usually compare three paths: an agent listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. Condition, timing and tenants decide which fits.

Listing works best for a well-kept house in a strong location when you can wait out showings. Cash fits deferred repairs, rentals with tenants, probate property or a firm closing date. Ask for an offer, set it against your likely net from a listing, and decline if it falls short. You owe nothing.

  1. Describe the house, its condition and any tenants.
  2. We review the details and make an offer.
  3. Accept, and a title company runs the closing and records the deed with the county.

Before the first call, collect the deed, the latest tax notice, any lease and your rental or short-term rental license if you have one. Missing items can usually be handled through the title company.

Frequently asked questions

What county is Salt Lake City in?

Salt Lake County, whose offices for assessing, tax collection and recording are right in the city.

When are Salt Lake City property taxes due?

By November 30. A bill left open on December 1 draws the greater of 2.5 percent or $10, cut to the greater of 1 percent or $10 when paid by January 31.

What is the property tax appeal deadline in Salt Lake County?

The later of September 15 and 45 days after your notice. Start from August 1 with form BE01 and proof of value, filed with the Board of Equalization.

Do I need a license to rent out my Salt Lake City house?

Yes, each rental location needs a valid business license, and the Good Landlord Program can trim per-unit fees by up to 95 percent.

Can I run a short-term rental in Salt Lake City?

Only in approved zoning districts and with a city license, for stays of two nights or more and no more than 200 rental nights per unit a year.

West Valley City at a glance

West Valley City is an inner suburb on the northwest side of the Salt Lake Valley and the second most populous city in Utah. Salt Lake City is to its north, South Salt Lake to the east, Magna to the west, and Taylorsville and Kearns to the south. The Oquirrh Mountains are west and the Jordan River forms the eastern edge. It covers roughly 35.5 to 35.9 square miles at about 4,304 feet.

The city incorporated in 1980 by merging four unincorporated communities: Hunter, Granger, Chesterfield and Redwood. It had 72,299 people in 1980, 129,480 in 2010 and 140,230 in 2020, an 8.3% rise over the last decade. The July 2025 estimate at the top of this page is 137,491, a little below the 2020 count.

Areas of the city and their houses

The city is usually described in three areas, and the age of the houses differs among them. These descriptions rest on 2013 neighborhood data, so incomes and populations have shifted since.

  • East (Redwood, Chesterfield and East Granger): mostly brick ranch houses from the 1960s and 1970s, near Valley Fair Mall and the Maverik Center. The Westshire area south of the mall has 160 mid-century modern homes from the 1960s and 1970s.
  • Central (West Granger and Hunter south of 3100 South, with Lakepark and Westlake Business Park to the north): includes the planned Highbury development in the northwest portion.
  • West (West Hunter, Woodhaven and Oquirrh): mostly planned developments from the 1990s and 2000s.

Median household income in 2013 was $42,512 in the East, $55,087 in the Central area and $64,356 in the West. A seller in the East is often selling a 50 or 60 year old brick ranch, so roof, plumbing and electrical updates drive the price.

Roads, transit and schools

Interstate 215, State Route 172 (5600 West) and State Route 171 (3500 South) are the main roads. West Valley Central station is on the TRAX Green Line, and the Utah Transit Authority runs an intermodal hub in the city. The 3500 South MAX bus line serves the area, and the Midvalley Express links West Valley Central and 2700 West to Taylorsville and on to Murray Central station.

The Granite School District covers the city and serves about 67,000 students across central Salt Lake County. Granger High School, which opened in 1958, and Hunter High School, which opened in 1990, are both in West Valley City. Charter schools include East Hollywood High School, American Preparatory Academy and Monticello Academy. A school boundary depends on the address, so ask the district to confirm it before you advertise the house.

Rental licensing and code rules

Every owner of a rental dwelling in West Valley City must hold a current city business license. An owner with several units needs only one license if they give the city a complete, current list of the units and pay the fees. When a property has more than one owner, each is jointly and severally liable for the fees and any penalties.

The code also sets a rental nuisance standard: more than two police calls for one rental unit in 12 months counts as excessive. An unresolved notice of violation is one with no recorded notice of compliance. The city's ordinance enforcement division handles abatement of unsightly or hazardous property and rental licensing.

  • Confirm your rental license is current before listing.
  • Clear any open notice of violation and record the notice of compliance.
  • Gather the unit list if you own more than one rental in the city.

Property tax in Salt Lake County

The county wants its property tax by November 30, and anything still unpaid on December 1 is delinquent. Notices come by November 1. The appeal window lasts 45 days and runs from August 1 to September 15. In late May the county sells parcels that are more than five years delinquent.

With Utah's 45% residential exemption, a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value. A second residence or vacant house is taxed at the full amount, which is worth checking if you have already moved out.

Recording your deed

The place to file is the Salt Lake County Recorder, 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, and the flat fee is $40.00. Include the parcel number and the grantee's mailing address, and have the deed notarized. That same office holds the ownership records the city checks when it identifies an owner for code and licensing.

After closing, the title company normally files the deed. For an inherited house, bring the old deed to the title company so the chain of ownership is clear before the sale.

Weather and wear on older houses

Salt Lake City, the nearest long-term station, averages a July high of 94.0 degrees and a January high of 38.6, with about 15.5 inches of precipitation and strong winter inversions. That climate keeps steady wear on roofs and on heating and cooling systems, and it shows most in houses that are decades old. An inspector will check the roof, the furnace and air conditioner, the electrical panel and the plumbing, and each one can become a point in price talks.

Selling with taxes owed or a tenant

Owing property tax does not stop a sale, since the title company takes the balance out of your proceeds and splits the current year's tax with the buyer. Still, do not let it slide. Five or more years of delinquency can put a parcel in the May tax sale, and options narrow fast by then.

For a rental, buyers will ask about the license, the unit list and any earlier notice of violation, so settle those items first. A tenant in place can slow a regular listing, because showings need notice and some buyers want to move in. A cash buyer can often close around the lease or after the tenant leaves. Raise it when you request an offer.

Selling a West Valley City house

You have three paths: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer. Listing suits a house in good shape and a seller willing to sit through showings. A cash sale suits an older ranch needing updates, a rental with code problems, or an inherited house nobody wants to look after.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses here as they stand. Ask for an offer, look at how we reached it, and make your own call. Keep the deed, the latest tax notice and any rental license handy to save time. We can set the closing date around your move, and the title company handles the deed filing and the tax split.

What county is West Valley City in?

Salt Lake County. Its offices in Salt Lake City handle the tax bill, valuation appeals and recording of deeds.

When are property taxes due in West Valley City?

The due date is November 30, and a balance still unpaid on December 1 is delinquent. Notices are mailed by November 1.

Do I need a business license to rent out a house in West Valley City?

Yes. Owners of rental dwelling units must hold a current city business license, and multi-unit owners can use one license with a list of units.

Which school district serves West Valley City?

The Granite School District. Granger High School and Hunter High School are in the city.

Can I sell a West Valley City house that needs work?

Yes. Houses sell as-is all the time, and owners of older ranches often choose a cash sale so they skip repair bills before closing.

West Jordan at a glance

Holding down the southwest corner of the Salt Lake Valley, West Jordan runs from the Jordan River up toward the Oquirrh range. Its neighbors are Taylorsville and Kearns on the north, South Jordan on the south, and Sandy, Murray and Midvale on the east. The city spans about 31 to 32 square miles and sits a bit above 4,300 feet.

Population rose from 68,336 in 2000 to 103,712 in 2010 and 116,961 in 2020, which ranks third in Utah. The July 2025 estimate shown above is 116,812, so the climb has stopped. The city was incorporated on January 10, 1941. It counted 27,192 people in 1980, and most of the housing was built after that.

Local figureValue
2020 census population116,961
2020 households35,044
2020 housing units36,247, with 3.3% vacant
Property tax due dateNovember 30
Recording fee per recording$40.00

Homeowner vacancy was 0.6% and rental vacancy 7.2% in 2020, so few owner-occupied houses sat empty.

Hillside lots versus river-side blocks

Welby, Copper Hills and Jordan Hills climb the Oquirrh foothills in the west. Views and drainage there are nothing like the level streets near the river, and shoppers compare the two areas.

Three things come up most on hillside lots:

  • Foundation cracks, and where rain and snowmelt run.
  • Roof age, since snow and summer sun both wear shingles.
  • How old the furnace and air conditioner are.

How much earthquake risk a house carries depends on nearby hazards and the year it was built, so some buyers ask about foundation age and retrofits. The Salt Lake City weather station, the closest with a long record, averages a January high of 38.6 degrees and low of 24.2, and a July high of 94.0 and low of 68.2. It gets about 15.5 inches of precipitation and roughly 52 inches of snow a year, and strong winter inversions trap air in the valley.

Roads, transit and school districts

I-15 skirts the east edge of the city and I-215 bends to the northeast. Bangerter Highway runs through the middle and Redwood Road through the east. The Mountain View Corridor has ten lanes and exits at 7800 South, 9000 South and Old Bingham Highway; its first phase opened December 15, 2012. TRAX light rail started running August 7, 2011, and six stops are inside West Jordan.

How close a house sits to a rail stop or an on-ramp is something buyers ask about early. Homes along Bangerter Highway or Redwood Road may have traffic noise, and homes a short walk from a station attract commuters.

The Jordan School District serves most of West Jordan, while two small northern pockets belong to Granite School District. West Jordan has 16 elementary schools, four middle schools and two high schools, West Jordan High and Copper Hills High. A house near a boundary can feed a different school than the neighbor across the street, so ask the district to confirm the boundary for your address.

Rental licensing and code enforcement

A rental in West Jordan requires a General Business License plus a Rental Dwelling application. Owners may also join the city's voluntary Good Landlord Program: finish a four-hour class, keep a signed agreement, a written lease and rental applications on file, and the fee is discounted. The class has to be retaken every four years.

The city expects at least one free off-street parking space for every rental unit, and it reports that single-family rentals generate 78% more police and fire calls each year than owner-occupied homes. Code enforcement is located at 8000 S. Redwood Road and answers at 801-569-5000. Complaints can be filed through the Report a Problem form on the city website.

If the house is a rental, make sure the license is current before you sell and any open code complaint is cleared, so neither turns up during a buyer's review. A buyer or lender may ask for the license number, the lease and a list of recent repairs, and having them ready shortens the back-and-forth.

Property tax: what you owe and when

The Salt Lake County tax year follows a fixed order:

  • January 1: your property's value is fixed as of this date.
  • By July 22: valuation notices arrive in the mail.
  • August 1 to September 15: you may appeal to the Board of Equalization.
  • By November 1: tax notices go out.
  • November 30: payment is due. From December 1 an unpaid balance is delinquent.

A home that is your primary residence gets Utah's 45% exemption on up to one acre, so only 55% of market value is taxed. A second home or an empty house is taxed at 100%. Moved out but still the owner? Check which rate your bill uses before you list, since a buyer's lender will see it.

Recording the deed at the county

Deeds are filed with the Salt Lake County Recorder, 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Here is what the office expects:

  • A flat $40.00 per recording, plus $2.00 for each legal description beyond ten.
  • The parcel number on the deed.
  • The grantee's mailing address.
  • A notary acknowledgment.

Your title company normally files for you at closing. When a house moves through a family or an estate, bring the deed and the latest tax notice so names and the parcel number line up first.

Choosing how to sell

Hiring an agent brings yard signs, weeks of showings and a closing date that hinges on the buyer's lender, and it suits a sound house and an owner with time. Going it alone saves the commission but leaves pricing, marketing and paperwork to you. Taking a cash offer means trading some price for speed and certainty. It fits best when the house has deferred repairs, a tenant, a late mortgage or an estate attached.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses across Utah, including West Jordan, in their current condition. We show how an offer is calculated, you take whatever time you need, and the decision is yours. Before you call, collect the deed, your last tax notice, any rental license and any loan statement.

Selling with taxes or tenants in place

An unpaid tax balance does not block a sale. It is deducted from your proceeds at closing, and the buyer shares the current year's bill. A tenant adds a layer: the rental should satisfy the city's rules, and the lease terms need to be clear before you talk with buyers. If a tenant, back taxes or repairs would stall an ordinary listing, a cash sale can be easier.

Begin with the deed and the latest county notice, and phone the Recorder or Treasurer if a figure looks off.

Frequently asked questions

What county is West Jordan, UT in?

Salt Lake County. Everything from the tax bill to a valuation appeal to deed recording is handled by county offices in Salt Lake City.

When are property taxes due in West Jordan?

Payment is due by November 30, and a balance still open on December 1 is delinquent. Notices are sent before November 1.

Does West Jordan require a rental license?

Yes. Landlords need a General Business License and a Rental Dwelling application. The Good Landlord Program is voluntary and gives a discounted fee to owners who finish the required class.

Which school district is West Jordan in?

The Jordan School District serves most of West Jordan, while two small northern pockets belong to Granite School District.

Can I sell my West Jordan house without repairs?

Yes. You are not obliged to repair anything first. A cash buyer accepts the house as it stands, and you decide once the offer is in front of you.

Provo at a glance

Provo is the Utah County seat, about 43 miles south of Salt Lake City on the eastern shore of Utah Lake. It spans 44.19 square miles, of which 41.69 are land and 2.50 are water, at roughly 4,550 feet, with Orem to the north and Springville to the south. ZIP codes run 84601 through 84606.

Interstate 15 crosses the west side, US 89 (State Street) runs northwest to southeast, and US 189 ties State Street, I-15, BYU and Orem together. The whitewashed Y on the mountain is the city's best-known landmark. For a seller, location relative to those roads, the campus and a transit stop is usually the first thing a buyer or tenant asks about, so put it near the top of any description.

Provo is mostly renters

Only 39.4% of homes are lived in by their owners, a low share that reflects the huge student population around BYU. The median age was 23.8 at the 2020 census. The city counted 115,162 residents then, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 114,527.

Since so many houses are rentals, a Provo seller often has a tenant, a lease or a school-year calendar to plan around. BYU enrolls over 30,000 students, and academic calendars affect when rentals turn over and when houses sell.

An old city with mixed housing

Fort Utah, founded in 1849 by 33 Mormon families, was the start of Provo. The city incorporated in April 1850 and was renamed for the trapper Etienne Provost. Brigham Young Academy, the forerunner of BYU, was founded in 1875, and orchards once earned Provo the name Garden City.

Housing here spans many decades, so condition varies a lot from street to street. The age of the roof, furnace and cooling equipment often comes up in a buyer's inspection. Annual precipitation is about 17.2 inches near BYU.

Trains, buses and the airport

Provo is the southern end of the FrontRunner commuter rail line, running since December 10, 2012. The Provo Intermodal Center brings together rail, local UTA buses and Greyhound, and Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at the station daily. UVX bus rapid transit, run jointly with Orem, runs toward Utah Valley University. Provo Municipal Airport is Utah's second-busiest by aircraft movements. Mean commute time is 18.4 minutes.

Accessory apartments and rental licenses

Provo allows one accessory dwelling unit on a lot with a one-family detached home, and the owner must live in the main house or the unit. The rules are in section 14.30.030 of the city code and carry real weight for anyone selling a house with a basement or garage apartment.

  • A rental dwelling license under Chapter 6.26 is required and renewed every year.
  • The license expires one year after approval or when the property is transferred, whichever comes first.
  • A deed restriction describing how the unit is built and occupied is recorded with the Utah County Recorder.
  • The owner must show the home is the primary residence with at least two documents, such as a driver license, vehicle registration, voter card or latest tax return.
  • No more than three adults, related or not, plus their minor children, may live in the unit.

Because the license ends on transfer, a buyer must apply again. Utah courts have upheld owner-occupancy requirements for renting an accessory unit, in Anderson v. Provo City (2005 UT 5), a case about accessory apartments in single-family zones near BYU. Cities may require a business license for short-term rentals but cannot ban a listing on an online platform.

Detached accessory units

Before state law S.B. 284, Provo allowed detached accessory dwellings only in specific overlay zones. The new statute reaches parcels of 11,000 square feet or larger with a single-family home. A policy proposal would cap accessory structures at 40 percent of the parcel, and the city has published a map of projected new eligibility. If a detached unit is part of your plans or your buyer's, check the current rule with Provo City first. Rules in this area are changing, and a promise made to a buyer today could be wrong next year, so get the answer in writing from the city if a detached unit affects the price.

School districts

Provo has its own Provo School District, with 13 elementary schools, two middle schools and three high schools. Alpine School District covers a small section of the city. Provo is outside the three new districts that replace Alpine in 2027, so its boundaries stay as they are. Parents will still ask which school an address feeds, so confirm it with the district.

Property tax in Utah County

Utah County does the assessing and billing, and its Auditor works in Provo itself at 100 East Center Street, Suite 3600. Expect a valuation notice at the end of July. If you dispute the market value, the Board of Equalization takes appeals until September 15, online, by email, by mail or in person. Tax notices arrive mid to late October.

Thanks to the 45% exemption, a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value if someone lives in it at least 183 consecutive days a year. A full-time tenant counts. A vacant or part-time rental is secondary and pays on full value, a rule that touches many Provo owners. The Treasurer, at 801-851-8255, gives payoff amounts on delinquent tax.

Selling a Provo house for cash

People call us about a house with tenants, a rental whose license lapsed, an inherited property or a place that needs repairs.

  2. We go through it and name a price that reflects condition.
  3. Agree, and an escrow or title company schedules closing.
  4. The county files the deed and you are paid.

We buy as-is, so there are no repairs or cleaning. Timing around leases and the school year is something we can plan with you.

Paperwork to gather

Gather the deed, the newest tax notice, any lease and rent roll, and for a house with an accessory unit, the rental dwelling license and recorded deed restriction. The title company will say what else it wants. Even a short list of what you hold speeds up the first call, and most gaps can be closed as the sale proceeds. If a tenant plans to leave at the end of a school term, tell us that date so closing can be set around it.

Can I sell a Provo house that has an accessory apartment?

Yes. The city wants an owner-occupied home and a rental dwelling license, and since the license ends at transfer, the buyer applies for a new one. We purchase the house as it stands.

Does the Provo rental license carry over to a new owner?

No. Per city code, it expires a year after approval or when the property transfers, whichever is first. The new owner applies.

What is the deadline to appeal Provo property taxes?

Appeal to the Utah County Board of Equalization by September 15. Later filings, through March 31, need to meet extra criteria.

Which county office records a Provo deed?

That is the Utah County Recorder, 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300 in Provo. Staff there don't draft papers, advise on law or search titles.

Why is Provo's owner-occupancy rate so low?

At 39.4% for 2020 to 2024 it reflects a big student population around BYU, with a median age of 23.8, which makes many houses rentals.

Selling a house in St. George

Utah's southwest corner, right at the Arizona line, is home to St. George, the Washington County seat. The city lies along Interstate 15 at 2,530 feet, roughly 118 miles northeast of Las Vegas and 300 miles south-southwest of Salt Lake City. Zion National Park is to the east and Snow Canyon State Park is close to town.

Residents numbered 49,728 in 2000 and 95,342 in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 108,713. About 13,000 people arrived in five years, which is why so many houses are newer. Retirees are a big part of the picture too, with 21.8% of residents age 65 or older, so downsizers and heirs selling an inherited house are common.

Housing and income rows cover 2020 to 2024. About two in three homes are owner-occupied. Read the median value as a survey number, not an offer on your house.

Desert heat and your house

Buyers here check the heat defenses first. Monthly averages climb from 42.1 degrees in December to 87.8 degrees in July, and around 60 afternoons a year hit 100 degrees or more. The all-time high was 118 degrees on July 4, 2007.

Yearly precipitation is only about 9 inches, with 1.4 inches of snow on average. Even so, close to 60 mornings fall to freezing or colder, and pipes in a poorly insulated home can suffer.

  • Air conditioners and roofs wear fastest, so inspectors ask how old they are.
  • Stucco, window seals and flat roofs that have baked in the sun may hide damage you cannot see from the curb.
  • A house close to the Santa Clara River or a wash shares its flood history. The January 2005 flood destroyed 28 homes along the river, so drainage is a fair question.

Water rules and landscaping

Water is a live issue across the county. A 2022 ordinance from the regional water conservancy district bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial, institutional and industrial developments and limits grass at new homes.

Cities do the enforcing, from water-waste complaints to metering data and penalties. Heavy users have paid an added fee since 2023, and that revenue funds rebates for swapping grass for water-efficient landscaping. The district projected savings of nearly 11 billion gallons over ten years.

With a big lawn, check with the city or your water provider before paying for landscaping you hope will help the sale.

Neighborhoods, roads and schools

Named areas organize how buyers think about the city: Downtown, Bloomington, Entrada, Green Valley, Little Valley, Red Cliffs, Snow Canyon, Sunbrook, Sunriver, The Ledges, Tonaquint and Desert Hills. Each has its own character, so name yours in the listing.

  • Interstate 15 runs northeast to southwest through the city.
  • State Route 7, the Southern Parkway, runs east and west along the south edge, and SR-8, SR-34 and SR-18 also serve the city.
  • The regional airport in the southeast offers flights on American, Delta and United, all operated by SkyWest.
  • SunTran runs seven fixed bus routes.

High schools in the county school district include Desert Hills, Dixie, Pine View, Snow Canyon and Crimson Cliffs. Newcomers with children usually want to know which one an address feeds.

Due dates and penalties

The county's property tax deadline is November 30, whether or not a notice reaches you. The tax attaches to the property rather than to its owner, so an unpaid bill follows the house to a new owner.

Late payment is delinquent under Utah Code section 59-2-1331, with a 2.5% penalty or $10, whichever is greater. Settling everything by January 31 reduces it to 1%. The treasurer takes partial payments of $10 or more per parcel at any time, and each May the clerk-auditor sells properties delinquent for at least five years.

At closing the title company splits the bill, and the settlement statement shows what each side owes.

Exemptions and appeals

A primary residence earns a 45% exemption on up to one acre. Rental homes can qualify, but vacation homes and time-shares cannot, so a second home in St. George is taxed on its full value. The Washington County assessor can say how your parcel is classified.

  • Treasurer: 111 East Tabernacle St., St. George, (435) 301-7720.
  • Auditor: (435) 301-7220. Lose before the county Board of Equalization and you can go on to the Utah State Tax Commission using Form TC-194, filed with the auditor within 30 days of the decision.

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid balance must be cleared at or before closing, and that is routine. The title company treats it as a payoff, deducts it from what you receive and passes clean title to the buyer. Phone the treasurer for today's figure and get it in writing so it lines up with the closing statement.

Closing day and what to bring

Once you accept an offer, a title company searches the ownership record, confirms the tax status and prepares a settlement statement. You sign the deed and closing papers, any mortgage is paid off from the proceeds and the deed is recorded with the county.

Bring a photo ID, the keys and any remotes or gate codes. If the house has a pool, a casita or an irrigation controller, write down how it works for the next owner. A short list like that is a courtesy buyers remember.

What a cash sale skips

The problems we hear are practical: an air conditioner or roof on its last legs, a yard that is costly to water, an heir living out of state, or a house that is miserable to show in July.

Selling for cash avoids the prep work of a listing. The house is bought in its current condition, so the roof, the AC and the yard stay as they are. Describe the property, receive an offer and name your closing date, and a title company handles the paperwork. Put the number beside a listing's likely result. Nothing requires you to accept.

For an inherited house or an owner who lives elsewhere, collect the deed or probate papers, the utility account details and contact information for whoever will sign. This keeps the title company from chasing paperwork and speeds up the date you can close.

How many people live in St. George, Utah?

The estimate is 108,713 for July 1, 2025, compared with 95,342 in the 2020 census. It is the largest city in Washington County.

When are St. George property taxes due?

November 30 every year. Later payments are delinquent and draw a 2.5% or $10 penalty, whichever is greater, cut to 1% when paid in full by January 31.

Who pays the property tax when a St. George house sells?

The title company splits it at closing. You pay for the days you owned the house, and the buyer pays the rest. Any unpaid balance is cleared at or before closing.

Does St. George have special water or landscaping rules?

Yes. A 2022 water district ordinance limits grass at new homes and bans nonfunctional grass at new commercial and industrial sites, and a heavy-use fee started in 2023. Check with the city about your lot.

Can I sell a St. George house that needs repairs or has tenants?

Yes. We take houses as they are, including those with old repairs, heat-damaged roofs or tenants. Describe the house and you will get an offer you can turn down.

Lehi housing in brief

Lehi sits at the northern end of Utah Valley in Utah County, covering about 28 square miles at roughly 4,561 feet. The population climbed from 19,028 in 2000 to 47,407 in 2010 and 75,907 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 95,313. The median age was 26.2 in 2020, and about 39.5 percent of residents were under 18, so family-sized houses are the norm. An older home in the original grid looks very different from a subdivision built a few years ago.

Winters are cold, with a January mean low near 16 degrees, and precipitation averages around 12 inches. Dry air does not spare water lines and older furnaces from the cold, and buyers notice both.

Old Lehi and the original grid

Pioneers settled the area in fall 1850 at a place called Dry Creek, and Lehi City was incorporated on February 5, 1852. The town stayed small for a century, with a census low of 2,733 in 1940 and only 8,475 in 1990. The Lehi Main Street Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Lehi Roller Mills, built by a farmers' cooperative in 1906, appeared in the 1984 film Footloose. A house in the old core often has older wiring, older plumbing and unusual lot lines, so expect inspection questions that a newer subdivision home would not face.

Jobs and timing

Lehi shifted from farming to a technology economy. Micron's chip plant became IM Flash Technologies, and Texas Instruments announced its purchase of the facility in June 2021. Adobe, Ancestry.com, Vivint, Microsoft and Oracle also have a presence. Ancestry.com has been headquartered here since 2016, the first hospital opened in June 2015, and Thanksgiving Point draws about 1.45 million visitors a year.

Owners who bought during a hiring wave can hit a layoff, a remote work change or an offer elsewhere. Timing becomes the problem, since the mortgage payment keeps coming while the house waits for a buyer.

Interstate 15 passes through Lehi with five exits, which is why many households chose the city. A house far from the interstate may draw a different buyer than one near the Corporate Center on Traverse Mountain.

Schools in transition

Alpine School District, which includes Lehi High and Skyridge High, will cease to exist in July 2027. Three new districts will replace it, and one is named Aspen Peaks. Check the boundary for the exact property with the district or the city before you tell a buyer which schools apply. Mountainland Technical College has a Lehi campus.

Permits, inspections and irrigation

The Building and Inspections Department issues every permit, and open permits or unfinished work can delay a closing. Applications go through an online portal, and the current codes include the 2021 I-Codes and the 2020 National Electrical Code with Utah amendments.

  • Have the work ready first, because re-inspection fees apply if a project clearly is not.
  • Look up status by permit number, site address or subdivision and lot.

Lehi also runs a pressurized irrigation system that supplies untreated water for yards and city fire hydrants. A city ordinance bars irrigation water use after October 15, and owners turn the connection on and off each year. Buyers from elsewhere often ask how the yard is watered, so explain the connection and watering schedule up front. Lehi City is at 131 N 100 E, phone (385) 201-1000.

A valuation notice is not a tax bill. The amounts due appear in the October notice, so a seller closing in the fall should ask the title company how that year's taxes will be prorated.

Recording the deed

Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder in Provo. The fee is $40 per document, and a state change added $5 to county recording fees, so ask for the current total before closing.

Does the primary residence exemption follow the house?

No. Utah takes 45 percent off the market value of a primary home, leaving 55 percent taxable, and the owner must live there at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year.

After a sale or deed transfer, the new owner files Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15. Counties cannot take late filings, and a buyer who misses the date can be taxed on full market value for that year. Rental owners file a residential declaration signed by all owners instead, and second or vacation homes do not qualify.

Telling your buyer about that date in advance avoids a surprise tax bill after a fall closing.

The title and recording steps are the same as in any sale, but the buyer needs no lender approval. A title company searches for liens, the parties sign, and the deed is recorded in Provo.

  • Compare the offer and closing date with a listing plan.

  • Sign and receive the proceeds after payoffs and prorated taxes.

This path suits owners who inherited a Lehi house, are behind on payments, or hold a house that needs work they do not want to finance.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer needs no lender, so there is no appraisal gap and no list of repairs required by a bank. You do not stage rooms or hold open houses. The house is bought as it stands, including an aging furnace or an unfinished project, and you help choose the closing date. Any open permit still has to be cleared, so ask the building department what is on file for your address.

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid taxes come out of your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for the balance and share it with the title officer. If the house closes in the fall, request the proration figure early, because the October notice changes the numbers.

By 5:00 pm on November 30. The county mails tax notices in October, and a valuation notice is not a bill.

Past notices have listed September 15. Check the notice you receive, since the date printed on it governs.

Will Alpine School District still serve Lehi?

Not after July 2027. Three new districts will replace it, so confirm the district for a specific address before telling buyers.

Orem's location and street layout

Orem is a Utah County city roughly 45 miles down the interstate from Salt Lake City, close to where Utah Lake meets the valley's east shore. It spans 18.57 square miles at roughly 4,767 feet, with Provo to the east and south, Vineyard to the west and Lindon to the north.

Two roads organize the map. Interstate 15 runs down the west side with four interchanges inside the city, and US 89 (State Street) cuts through the middle from northwest to southeast. Cross streets including 800 North (Canyon Parkway), 1600 North, University Parkway and Geneva Road carry state route numbers. Shoppers tend to measure a house by its distance to State Street, University Parkway and the freeway, so know those numbers before you list.

Early farmers spread their homes along the old territorial highway, now State Street, and that pattern still shows. Older lots near State Street and the original grid differ a lot from the newer tracts built later.

Orem housing numbers

The 2020 census put Orem at 98,129 people, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 95,214. Only Utah's four biggest cities are larger, and owners occupy a bit over half of the homes.

Types of homes in Orem

The mix runs from detached houses to townhomes to apartment buildings, and the city posts the breakdown. Of 29,593 occupied units in the 2021 American Community Survey, 17,913 (60.5%) were owner-occupied and 11,680 (39.5%) were rented.

  • Single-family homes: 16,509 units, or 55.8% of occupied housing

Accessory apartments

Orem permits an accessory apartment within a house, with one condition: the owner occupies either the main residence or the apartment. The city counted 752 legal accessory apartments as of June 2023, with 30 added in 2022 and 23 more in the first half of 2023.

That condition comes up at sale time. An apartment that was never registered, or one a past owner rented out from somewhere else, invites questions during a buyer's inspection. Detached accessory units are a newer topic under state law S.B. 284. Orem's proposed response would keep them out of front yards and bar short-term rental use, and the law reaches lots of 11,000 square feet or more. Before telling a buyer a detached unit is possible, find out from city planners where the rules stand.

Getting around Orem

FrontRunner has a station west of I-15, and a pedestrian bridge connects it to the UVU campus. UVX, a bus rapid transit line run jointly with Provo, connects Orem Central Station, UVU and University Parkway toward Provo. Average commute time for Orem workers is 20.1 minutes.

If your house is a short walk from the station or a UVX stop, say so in the listing.

School district change coming in 2027

Today Alpine School District covers Orem. On July 1, 2027 it is dissolved, and Orem goes to the new Timpanogos district with Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard. Voters approved the split in the 2024 general election, board members were elected in 2025 and superintendents were hired in 2026.

Parents will ask which district a house belongs to, and the answer is changing. Look up your exact address on the boundary map before you quote one.

Utah County property tax

The county sends each Orem owner a Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Changes near the end of July. To dispute the market value, file with the county Board of Equalization by September 15. The actual tax bill arrives between the middle and end of October.

A primary home earns a 45% residential exemption, which means the tax is figured on 55% of market value. To qualify, someone has to live there for at least 183 consecutive days a year: the owner, a relative or a full-time tenant. A rental without a full-time eligible occupant is treated as secondary and taxed on the full amount.

Sandy is a city in Salt Lake County, tucked against the Wasatch Mountains, roughly 13 miles from downtown Salt Lake. The 2020 census counted 96,904 people, a rise of 10.8 percent over the 87,461 counted in 2010. The real surge happened earlier. Sandy went from 6,438 residents in 1970 to 52,210 in 1980, and a big portion of today's houses went up in that stretch of fast building.

Think about that history before you pick an asking price. Roofs, furnaces and water heaters installed in the same years age together, and an inspector working for the buyer will check each one.

Sandy's eastern edge rises into the foothills. Its western edge is flat valley floor, and the Jordan River marks part of that boundary. Lots, views and drainage change from one side to the other, so visitors to a hillside home ask different things than visitors to a home by the river. Canyons School District has been the main district since the 2009-10 school year. Boundaries move now and then, so ask the district which school an address feeds before you promise anything to a buyer.

Roads and transit

Freeway access comes from I-15 on the western side, with exits at 9000 South, 10600 South and 11400 South. State Street is U.S. Route 89, parallel to the freeway, while State Route 209 goes east and west. Four TRAX Blue Line light rail stops sit inside Sandy.   • Sandy Expo at 9375 South
  • Sandy Civic Center at 10000 South
  • Crescent View at 11400 South

A short walk to a station or an easy hop to the freeway belongs near the top of your description. A house on a loud arterial street will draw comments about traffic, so decide ahead of time what you will say.

The Cairns redevelopment

The Cairns is the city center redevelopment plan, a 25-year effort covering about 1,100 acres. The master plan was adopted in January 2017 and divides the area into three villages: Central, South and East. The South Village includes City Hall and the Hale Centre Theatre, and the East Village is a transit-oriented area around the Sandy Civic Center TRAX station.

America First Field opened on October 8, 2008 and hosts Real Salt Lake and Utah Royals FC. We do not predict what projects like these do to home prices. The honest pitch is simple: a long-range plan and several big developments are under way near the middle of town, and buyers can decide what that is worth.

Foundation cracks, the canyon and the fault

Little Cottonwood Canyon gave Sandy its mining past and now leads to the Alta and Snowbird ski areas. Snow piles up on roofs there, so an older roof gets a close look.

The city is also part of the Wasatch Front, where the Wasatch Fault stretches about 240 miles in 10 segments, five of them active. Around 80 percent of Utahns live along it. On March 18, 2020 a 5.7 quake near Magna did moderate damage across the valley.

Hairline cracks in a foundation or chimney tend to appear in a buyer's inspection report. A cash buyer sees the house as it is today and prices the work into the offer, so you skip the contractor bids.

Sandy's city government runs building permits, code enforcement, trash pickup, a bulk waste program, recycling and utility billing, and it licenses pets and businesses. If you finished a basement or built a deck, call Community Development and ask whether that project needed a permit.

  • Check for code violations on the city's code violation page.

Salt Lake County does the assessing and billing for Sandy. Assessed value is set each January 1. Owner-occupied homes get a 45 percent exemption covering the buildings and as much as one acre. The bill must be paid by November 30.

Pay late and you owe 2.5 percent on top. Clear the full balance by January 31 and that charge shrinks to 1 percent. Parcels still unpaid after that go to the county tax sale in late May. When you sell partway through a year, ask your title company how the tax is split between you and the buyer, and get the number on paper before closing day.

Your valuation notice arrives in late July. The Board of Equalization hears appeals from August 1 through September 15, or for 45 days after the mailing when that runs later. Submit a BE01 form with proof, for example nearby sales, repair quotes or photos of damage.

Filing works online, by mail to 2001 South State Street, or at room N3-300 in the Government Center. Pull your proof together early so September is not a scramble.

Listing the usual way brings deep cleaning, repairs, photography, open houses, an appraisal and an inspection followed by repair demands. A cash offer cuts most of that out. You describe the property, we respond with an offer, and you choose the closing day that fits your move. A title company still handles the closing paperwork.

Gather a few items first: install dates for the roof, furnace and water heater, any permit records, a recent utility bill and, if a mortgage exists, the payoff amount from your lender. With those in hand the offer comes faster and fits the house better.

What closing day looks like

Once you accept an offer, a title company opens the file and searches the ownership record for liens or unpaid bills. You sign the deed and settlement papers, any mortgage balance is paid from the proceeds, and the remainder goes to you. The deed is recorded with the county, and you hand over the keys.

Bring a government photo ID and the garage and door openers. If tenants live there, bring copies of their leases. A quick walk through the rooms beforehand helps you remember what is staying and what is not.

List, sell by owner or take a cash offer?

Pick based on how the house looks and how fast you must move. A listing suits a tidy home and an owner who can live through weeks of showings.

A cash offer fits a home that needs work, an inherited property, a house with tenants, or a tight deadline. Ask for our number, set it beside what a listing would likely net you, and walk away if it does not work. It costs nothing to ask.

Sandy is in Salt Lake County, and the county offices handle assessments, tax bills and appeals.

What school district is Sandy in?

Canyons School District has been the main district since 2009-10. Ask the district about any particular address.

When are Sandy property taxes due?

The deadline is November 30. Anything unpaid is delinquent December 1, and paying everything by January 31 lowers the penalty to 1 percent.

How do I appeal my Sandy home's valuation?

Go to the Salt Lake County Board of Equalization from August 1 to September 15, or 45 days after your notice if that ends later. Bring the BE01 form and your proof of value.

Will a cash buyer take a Sandy house that needs repairs?

Yes. The offer reflects the house as it stands, so the roof, furnace or foundation can wait.

Ogden in brief

Ogden is the Weber County seat, about 40 miles north of Salt Lake City and 10 miles east of the Great Salt Lake. It covers 27.55 square miles and climbs from the valley floor to the Wasatch foothills on its east side. The 2020 census counted 87,321 residents.

The city splits into six districts. The North End holds West Ogden, Downtown and East Central, and the East side includes the East Bench and Shadow Valley. South Ogden, Roy, West Haven, Marriott-Slaterville, Farr West, Harrisville, Pleasant View and North Ogden border it.

About 61.3% of homes are owner-occupied, across 33,508 households. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $355,600, median gross rent is $1,216 and median household income is $72,575.

These are citywide medians. Mean travel time to work is 22.5 minutes.

A rail town with a long history

Ogden began as Fort Buenaventura, built in 1846 by the trapper Miles Goodyear a mile west of today's downtown. Captain James Brown bought it in November 1847 for $3,000, and the city incorporated on February 6, 1851. It later took the name of Peter Skene Ogden.

The city grew up as a rail hub, being the closest large city to Promontory Summit, where the first transcontinental railroad was joined in 1869. Freight still moves through, and FrontRunner commuter rail now carries riders to Salt Lake City and Provo. The National Park Service named Ogden a World War II Heritage City on September 17, 2024.

Older homes and historic districts

Ogden's historic districts include Historic 25th Street, Eccles Avenue and Jefferson Avenue. Union Station, Peery's Egyptian Theatre and the Ogden Nature Center are local landmarks.

The city's housing element, amended in 2022, reports that over 44 percent of Ogden's housing was built before 1940, against 27.2 percent in Weber County. That figure comes from an older section of the plan, so treat it as a rough guide. Still, a seller with a house from the early twentieth century should expect questions about wiring, plumbing, the roof and the foundation.

The same plan lists three projects approved as moderate-income housing actions: Lotus Riverwalk Phase 2 with 174 units, Meadowbrook with 48 and Capital Square with 176. It also describes the R-9 zone in the 9 Rails Creative District, which allows up to 29 units per acre, and cottage lots of 1,500 square feet within two blocks of the bus rapid transit route. New construction like this gives buyers more choices, so price your house against what is actually for sale nearby.

Winter, heat and the Wasatch Fault

Summers run hot and fairly dry, with highs often reaching 95 degrees, and winters bring snow from about late October or early November until around April. A roof and heating system that handle both matter to buyers. Average annual precipitation is 16.36 inches.

Ogden also lies along the Wasatch Fault. The Weber segment last produced a major earthquake roughly 200 to 700 years ago, and each active segment can generate a quake as large as about magnitude 7.5. An older house may merit a structural check before listing.

Which school district an address is in

Ogden City School District's boundary matches the city limits. Weber School District serves areas outside the city, even when those homes carry an Ogden mailing address. A listing that says Ogden therefore doesn't settle which district a house is in, so confirm it for the address. Buyers with children often ask, and a quick check with the district saves a misunderstanding later.

Trains, buses and the airport

FrontRunner links Ogden Central Station directly with Salt Lake City. The OGX bus line runs between that station and Weber State University, and other UTA routes reach Brigham City, Weber County and Davis County. Ogden-Hinckley Airport is Utah's busiest municipal airport, and Breeze Airways provides its only commercial service, with nonstop flights to Orange County, California.

Every residential rental in Ogden needs a license, and it is unlawful to occupy a rental without one. Applications are emailed to businesslicense@ogdencity.com. An invoice follows, and payment is required before the license is issued.

Short-term rentals face tighter limits under city code 15-13-38.

  • A sale voids a short-term rental license unless the new owner gets a new one within 90 days and before operating.
  • In R-1 zones only owner-occupied rentals are allowed, and a non-owner-occupied rental in a residential zone needs three years of continuous ownership.
  • Non-owner-occupied units are inspected every two years, and a revoked property is barred from short-term use for three years.
  • Occupancy is capped at two people per sleeping room, and parking must be on site.

If the house you are selling has been used as an Airbnb, check your license status before a buyer's agent asks. Because a sale voids the short-term license, tell a buyer who plans to continue the rental that they need to start the new application right away.

Appeals go to the Clerk/Auditor at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 320, and the valuation notice comes with an application. Any tax relief shows on the tax notice, not the valuation notice, so check the right document before you assume a break was applied.

Deeds are recorded with the Weber County Recorder, which charges $45 for the first page of a recording and nothing for additional pages, with $2 for each description over ten. Your title company normally pays these at closing and files the deed for you, so you will not usually stand in line at the counter.

A cash sale skips the listing, the buyer's loan and the appraisal. You describe the house, we make an offer based on its condition, and a title company handles signing and recording.

Ogden sellers often have older houses, rentals or inherited property, and many are not sure what to do first. The first step is just a conversation about the house. If you hold a rental license, bring it along, plus your latest tax notice, so we can go over the details before an offer.

The 2020 census counted 87,321 people in Ogden.

November 30 is the deadline to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, with a penalty of the greater of 1 percent or $10.

No. That district matches the city limits, while Weber School District serves areas outside it even if the address says Ogden.

Do I need a license to rent out a house in Ogden?

Yes, all residential rentals need one, and occupying an unlicensed rental is unlawful. For a short-term rental, a new owner has 90 days after a sale to get a new license.

South Jordan occupies the middle of the Salt Lake Valley, roughly 18 miles south of the capital, and slopes from the Jordan River up toward the Oquirrh foothills. Treat the median as a survey figure and not a quote for your address. A house with a worn roof, an unfinished basement or a dated kitchen sells under it, and a lakeview Daybreak home can sell over it.

Because the whole city falls inside one county, all three property offices belong to Salt Lake County. Jordan School District runs the public schools, including Bingham High and Herriman High.

Daybreak and the construction around it

Daybreak is a master-planned community of about 4,200 acres on the west side, started in 2004 by Kennecott Land. The remaining 1,300 undeveloped acres were sold to Larry H. Miller Group in 2022, and a new Downtown Daybreak opened in 2025 with the Salt Lake Bees ballpark as its anchor.

The city describes Downtown Daybreak as part of a Housing Transit Reinvestment Zone along the Mountain View Corridor, between two existing TRAX stations. If you live on the west side, plan for more building nearby for several more years, and be upfront about noise, traffic and showing schedules.

Roads, rail and schools

Commute questions come first from out-of-town buyers. Freeway I-15 skirts the east side, exiting at 10600 South and 11400 South, and Bangerter Highway cuts through the center with ramps at 9800, 10400 and 11400 South.

  • TRAX Red Line: three Daybreak stations, at South Jordan Parkway, South Jordan Downtown and Daybreak Parkway. The ride from Daybreak Parkway to downtown Salt Lake City takes about 60 minutes.
  • FrontRunner commuter rail: a station at 10200 South.
  • Charter and private options: Paradigm High, Early Light Academy, Hawthorne Academy, American Heritage and Stillwater Academy.

Short-term rentals and basement apartments

What is allowed hinges on the kind of property. Condos, townhouses, single-family houses and guest houses may host nightly stays, though a guest house first needs an approved accessory dwelling unit permit. A basement apartment is an internal ADU and cannot be rented nightly.

Did you ever advertise your finished basement online? A lender or inspector may raise it, and the space could only qualify as a long-term rental.

City code 5.04.100 makes business licenses non-transferable, and applications go through the city's online portal. Your license will not pass to the buyer, so be careful how you describe rental income.

Radon and earthquake risk

Inspectors raise both, and both are ordinary for homes in this part of Utah. The Wasatch Fault is roughly 240 miles long, and the odds of a magnitude 6.0 or stronger earthquake inside 50 years are estimated at 57%. In March 2020 a 5.7 quake near Magna damaged buildings across the valley.

Radon is a gas that seeps up from the ground. The state radon program reports elevated readings in one of every three Utah homes and sets the action level at 4 picocuries per liter. Testing is advised, and a result above that level may mean installing a mitigation system.

With a cash purchase as is, both just become part of the price conversation.

Due dates and penalties

The county sends the bill, and November 30 is the cutoff for paying this year's tax with no penalty. On December 1, any unpaid real property tax is delinquent.

  • Tax notices are mailed by November 1.
  • Late payers owe the greater of 2.5% or $10, which shrinks to 1% when the balance is cleared by January 31.

A primary residence is 45% exempt, which leaves 55% of market value as the taxable amount. The Treasurer's office is at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, Salt Lake City, phone (385) 468-8300. The Recorder, who files your deed, is in Suite N1-600 at (385) 468-8145.

Appealing your valuation

Appeals to the Board of Equalization are open from August 1 to September 15. Think your valuation is high? Collect nearby sales, repair quotes and photos of trouble spots such as an aging roof or a damaged basement before the window opens. A well-organized file is your best argument.

How a cash sale works in South Jordan

Selling for cash removes the loan, so nothing depends on a bank's appraisal or approval. Ask for an offer, let the buyer look over the property, and then name a closing date that suits your schedule.

A title or escrow company still handles the closing, and the Salt Lake County Recorder files the deed. Tax is split by days owned, so your share at closing follows how much of the year the house was yours. Expect questions about the roof, heating and cooling system and any finished basement, and dig up those records before you request offers.

Overdue taxes or a lien on the title are paid off from your proceeds when the sale closes, and the title company lists each amount for you.

What to gather before you sell

A little preparation shortens any sale. Pull your most recent property tax notice, the mortgage payoff amount if there is a loan, and any paperwork for work done on the house. If a basement or garage was finished, locate the permit. If a unit was rented, find the lease and note the deposit.

Also decide what stays. Appliances, window coverings and the garage door openers are all fair questions on closing day, and settling them early prevents last-minute friction.

Finally, talk to your lender or the title company about timing. If you have already bought another house, tell the buyer, because a flexible closing date, either soon or later, is often worth more to a stressed seller than a slightly higher price.

Problems sellers often run into

  • Basement or garage conversions built without a permit, which the city will not count as legal units.
  • A short-term rental history that conflicts with the rules for the property type.
  • Daybreak construction that changes noise, traffic and showing schedules.
  • High radon results that appear late in a financed sale.
  • A tight timeline because you have already bought another house.

Learn about any of these before the first showing, not after an offer. If one applies to you, say so when you ask for a cash offer so the number you receive already accounts for it.

Frequently asked questions

Is South Jordan in Salt Lake County?

Yes, all of it. Three county offices (Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder) deal with valuation, tax and deed, and the city's schools belong to Jordan School District.

When are South Jordan property taxes due?

Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. After that the tax is delinquent, though a balance cleared by January 31 only carries the 1% rate.

Can I use a basement apartment in South Jordan as an Airbnb?

No, a basement apartment is an internal ADU and the city bars it from nightly rental. Other property types, including a permitted guest house, can qualify under the license rules.

How many people live in South Jordan?

About 77,487 in the 2020 count, up from 50,418 in 2010.

Can I sell a South Jordan house that needs repairs?

Layton housing in brief

Layton is Davis County's largest city, on the northern Wasatch Front about 25 miles north of Salt Lake City and 15 miles south of Ogden. The 2020 count was 81,773 residents and the July 2025 estimate is 85,308. Hill Air Force Base sits on the northern edge, Clearfield and South Weber lie beyond it, and Kaysville and Syracuse border the city to the south and west.

The east side climbs toward the foothills and Adams Canyon, the middle follows I-15 where shopping and hotels cluster, and the west side runs flatter toward the lake wetlands. Housing arrived in waves, which means a single street can hold 1960s ramblers with homes from the 1990s and later subdivisions. Condition swings widely from block to block.

Lake effect snow and hot summers wear down roofs and furnaces, and an aging one tends to turn up on a buyer's inspection report. Owners of older houses often choose at that point between fixing things and selling as-is.

Hill Air Force Base and your timeline

Hill Field opened on November 7, 1940 and was renamed Hill Air Force Base on February 5, 1948. Its Ogden Air Logistics Complex provides engineering and logistics management for aircraft such as the F-35, F-16 and A-10, and units on base include the 75th Air Base Wing and the 388th and 419th Fighter Wings. Assignments, deployments and retirements keep local housing turning over.

If a transfer forces you out by a set day, a listing that may sit for weeks is a poor fit. Many cash buyers will close on a date you name.

Retail and hospitality cluster along I-15, including Layton Hills Mall, Restaurant Row, over 1,000 hotel beds and the Davis Conference Center. East Gate Business Park and a Weber State University campus add jobs and students.

Roads, rail and schools

I-15 runs through the center of town with exits at Antelope Drive, Hillfield Road and Layton Parkway. US-89 hugs the east edge near the foothills, SR-193 passes the base's south gate, and SR-177 serves the west. FrontRunner stops at Layton Station, built where the old Union Pacific depot stood. Homes near the station or an I-15 ramp suit commuters bound for Salt Lake City or Ogden.

Davis School District serves Layton. Layton High School opened in 1966 and Northridge High School in 1992, and the Northern Utah Academy for Math, Engineering and Science is an early college charter school partnered with Weber State. Buyers often ask which boundary a house falls in, so confirm the address with the district and do not rely on a listing description.

Parks that appeal to buyers include Layton Commons Park, Ellison Park and Legacy Park, plus the Edward A. Kenley Centennial Amphitheater and the Layton Utah Temple, dedicated on June 16, 2024.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Layton house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Code enforcement before you sell

Enforcement runs through the police department and centers on how the outside of a property looks. A buyer or lender who notices a violation can stall your sale, and unpaid cleanup bills can follow you.

Layton code ruleRequirement
Weeds and grass12 inches or shorter
Junk, appliances, tires, building materialsStored only inside a structure with walls and a roof
VehiclesRegistered, operable and parked on a hard surface
Expired registration, four months or moreVehicle removed or enclosed
Trees and bushesAt least 7 feet above sidewalks, 13 feet 6 inches above streets

First comes a 14-day courtesy notice. After a re-inspection, a Notice of Ordinance Violation can go to the City Attorney's Office. If an owner never cleans up, a judge can order the city to remove the violations and bill the owner plus an administrative fee.

Owners of vacant or inherited houses who live elsewhere can miss these notices. To learn whether anything is open, email codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov or call (801) 497-8300.

Valuation notices and appeals

Late July is when Davis County mails the valuation notice, and the appeal period ends in mid-September. Phone Tax Administration for the exact day before you file.

County commissioners double as the Board of Equalization. Market value is the only thing you can contest, and the filer must be the owner or an agent holding notarized authorization. Useful proof: closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales close to January 1, or documented errors in assessor records.

You will find Tax Administration at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, or at 801-451-3331 and taxadmin@daviscountyutah.gov. If you bought recently, your closing statement is strong support.

The primary residence exemption

Your main home gets a 45 percent break on market value, so 55 percent is taxable. To qualify, someone must live there for 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, and each household claims one exemption only.

The break stays with you, not the house. Buyers send Form TC-473A to the county Board of Equalization by September 15, and late forms are refused. Miss it and the same house can be taxed at 100 percent of value for a year, so give your buyer a heads-up.

How a cash sale works in Layton

The title steps match any other sale, minus the mortgage approval. The seller signs a purchase contract, a title company searches for liens, and the deed is recorded with the Davis County Recorder in Farmington.

  • Share the address, the condition and any deadline, such as a base transfer or a code notice.
  • Review the offer and the closing date the buyer proposes.
  • Sign the contract and let the title company clear liens, unpaid property taxes and any open code charges.
  • Sign the deed at closing and receive the proceeds after payoffs.

Davis County offers a Property Watch email alert that tells an owner when the title on a parcel changes. Sellers who live away from Layton, or who inherited a house, can sign up to hear about any change.

What a cash sale skips

Without a mortgage, you skip the lender's appraisal and any repair list it would demand. There are no open houses, no staging and no weeks of showings. You also pick the closing date, which helps a great deal when a transfer, a deployment or an inheritance sets the clock for you. The title company still checks for liens and prepares the deed.

Selling with taxes owed or open code charges

Open property taxes and code charges are paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask Tax Administration and the code enforcement office for current balances, then give both numbers to the title officer so your payout is clear before the signing.

Frequently asked questions

How big is Layton, Utah?

Layton is the largest city in Davis County. The 2020 count was 81,773 residents, with an estimate of 85,308 for July 2025.

Does Hill Air Force Base affect Layton home sales?

Yes, indirectly. The base borders Layton and is one of the largest employers in Utah, so moves and retirements regularly bring owners who need to sell or buy on a set schedule.

When are Davis County property tax valuation notices mailed?

At the end of July each year. Appeals close in mid-September, so confirm the exact date with Tax Administration at 801-451-3331.

Can code enforcement notices be fixed before selling a house in Layton?

Yes. Layton starts with a 14-day courtesy notice, and weeds, junk or an inoperable vehicle can often be cleared in that window. Email codeenforcement@laytoncityutah.gov to ask what is open on an address.

Does a buyer keep the primary residence exemption on a Layton house?

Not automatically. New owners must file Form TC-473A by September 15 to receive the 45 percent exemption, and a late filing can mean tax on full market value for that year.

Eagle Mountain and Utah County

Eagle Mountain is in northwest Utah County, in the flat Cedar Valley west and north of the Lake Mountains, and it belongs to the Provo-Orem metro area. The city covers about 50 square miles at roughly 4,885 feet. Because it is in Utah County, your tax bill, deed recording and property records all run through Provo. The county treasurer and recorder both work from the county building at 100 East Center Street.

The city grew fast: 2,157 residents in 2000, 21,415 in 2010, 43,623 in 2020 and an estimated 66,557 in mid-2025. Homes are mostly owner-occupied at 84.7%, the median home value is $518,100, median gross rent is $2,020, and the average household has 4.18 people. Data centers are the most visible employer here, and ongoing construction and hiring keep newcomers looking for homes.

Which school district will serve the house?

The Alpine School District serves Eagle Mountain now, and that changes on July 1, 2027, when the district splits into three. Eagle Mountain, Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort and Fairfield will form the Lake Mountain School District. Lehi, American Fork, Highland, Alpine and Cedar Hills go to Aspen Peaks, and Orem, Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard go to Timpanogos.

Current schools include eight elementary schools, Frontier Middle School and Cedar Valley High School, which opened in August 2019, plus charter schools such as The Ranches Academy, John Hancock Charter School and Rockwell Charter High School. If you sell during the transition, expect buyers to ask which district the address will land in, and send them to the district office for boundary maps.

Roads and weather

The main routes are SR-73, Pony Express Parkway, Eagle Mountain Boulevard and Ranches Parkway. The Mountain View Corridor segment linking the Salt Lake and Utah valleys was completed in December 2025, and UTA has run express bus Route 806 since 2008.

Rainfall is light, about 16.75 inches a year in the Ranches area. The city center is drier and cooler with colder nights, and the combined average July high is 90 degrees. Buyers usually ask for the roof's age, so have that date handy.

Accessory units and short-term rentals

Eagle Mountain allows accessory dwelling units, but not in townhomes, duplexes or apartments, and an ADU permit is required on top of any building permit.

  • The unit needs its own kitchen, bathroom and separate entrance.
  • The owner must live in either the main home or the ADU, with temporary absences allowed.
  • The site plan must show two off-street parking spaces.
  • The application fee is $230.
  • ADUs cannot be rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days.

Unpermitted units are treated as illegal until an application is approved. Short-term rentals of any kind also carry a 1% transient room tax under city code, with records kept for at least three years. Unpaid amounts add a 10% penalty and 12% annual interest, and the operator's business license can be revoked.

Property tax dates and deed recording

Utah County sets the calendar, and every date below comes from the county.

EventWhen

Mailed payments count if they carry a U.S. Post Office postmark, but a postage meter mark from an office does not. Utah also gives a 45% primary residential exemption, so tax is based on 55% of a primary home's value.

Deeds are recorded with the Utah County Recorder in Provo, which charges a $40 standard fee per document plus $2 for each description over ten. Credit and debit cards carry a 2.65% processing fee, while electronic checks do not.

Selling a house with an ADU or basement unit

Many Eagle Mountain houses have a finished basement, and some have a second unit. Whether you can sell it as a legal rental depends on the permit. A unit with an approved ADU permit, its own kitchen, bathroom and separate entrance, and two off-street parking spaces on the site plan is a selling point. A unit without one is treated as illegal until an application is approved, and a lender may refuse to count it.

If you did apply, keep the receipt or the approval. If you rented the house for stays under 30 days, keep the transient room tax records for at least three years, because unpaid amounts add a 10% penalty and 12% annual interest. A buyer's title company may ask about both, and having the answer ready helps the sale.

You do not have to settle every question before you sell for cash. You do need to describe the unit honestly, so the buyer can price the house for what it is.

Appeals, taxes and the closing statement

If you think your valuation is too high, the Board of Equalization deadline is September 1, set by the county. After that date the value stands for the year, so a closing in the fall cannot reopen it. The Auditor's notice, mailed around July 22, is the paper to keep.

At closing the title company divides the year's tax between you and the buyer and pays any unpaid balance from your proceeds. Ask for that line to be shown separately on the closing statement. If you mail a payment before closing, use a U.S. Post Office postmark, since a postage meter mark from an office does not count.

What to gather before you talk to a buyer

A short folder of papers saves days later. Start with the parcel number from your Utah County tax notice, since every county lookup depends on it.

  • The most recent tax notice and proof of payment.
  • The ADU permit or the application receipt, if the house has a second unit.
  • Transient room tax records, if you ever rented the house for stays under 30 days.
  • Any HOA contact, loan payoff details and the roof's age.

Pull any HOA documents too. Buyers often want to know about dues and rules before they sign, and a quick call to the HOA contact gets you the figures you need.

If you are unsure whether an ADU or a basement unit was ever permitted, ask the city before you list. The answer decides whether a financed buyer can close.

How does a cash sale work in Eagle Mountain?

A cash sale means no mortgage underwriting, so closing depends on title work alone.

  2. We review the property and nearby sales.
  3. You accept or decline the offer.
