  5. The deed is recorded in Provo and you are paid at closing.

A house with an unpermitted ADU or an unfinished basement can be hard for a financed buyer to close on. With no lender involved, the condition of the house is between you and us.

Utah County. Property taxes and recording go through the county offices in Provo.

November 30. Delinquent parcels are charged starting December 1.

Which school district will Eagle Mountain be in after 2027?

The Lake Mountain School District, which replaces Alpine School District on July 1, 2027 and also covers Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort and Fairfield.

Can I rent my Eagle Mountain basement apartment short term?

No, not as an ADU. ADU rentals must run at least 30 consecutive days, and other short-term rentals owe a 1% transient room tax.

Millcreek became a city in 2016

Voters approved incorporation on November 3, 2015, and Millcreek became a city on December 28, 2016. A 2012 attempt had failed with about 40 percent support. For years before that the area was a county township, created by Salt Lake County in 2002 to give residents a stronger voice in planning and to keep neighboring cities from annexing it.

The first mayor and council took office in 2016. City hall is therefore young, and some rules, ADU policy included, are still being refined. Ask the city for the current version before you rely on any summary, this page included.

Millcreek housing and population

The city is mostly residential and fairly settled. Settlement dates to 1848, the area stayed rural until after World War II, and suburban building then pushed south from Salt Lake City until most of it was built out by the 1980s. Expect a lot of postwar through 1980s houses, where a buyer's inspector looks first at the roof, plumbing and wiring.

Millcreek measureFigure
Population, 202063,380
Households25,111
Housing units26,650, with 5.8% vacant
Owner-occupied rate61.4%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$627,200
Median gross rent$1,492

The median value is a citywide figure. It does not predict what a specific house will bring, particularly a hillside lot or one with an extra unit.

Where Millcreek sits and its four community councils

Millcreek lies south of Salt Lake City and South Salt Lake and north of Murray and Holladay, with Mill Creek Canyon rising directly to the east. Four community councils divide it.

  • Canyon Rim, in the northeast, has steeper ground.
  • East Mill Creek sits near the mouth of the canyon.
  • Mount Olympus takes in Olympus Cove in the eastern foothills.
  • The Millcreek area covers the western and central parts, which are the most densely developed.

Five ZIP codes cover the city: 84106, 84107, 84109, 84117 and 84124. Because a mailing address alone can't tell you whether a house is inside Millcreek, look up the parcel record.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Millcreek house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Earthquake, slope and flood rules

Millcreek has a sensitive lands ordinance covering faults, liquefaction areas, steep slopes and the Mill Creek floodplain, along with avalanche and rockfall zones, alluvial fans, stream corridors, ridgelines and the wildland and urban interface. Mount Olympus debris flow areas roughly track slopes steeper than 30 percent.

Depending on the hazard, a project may need a fault survey, a soils study or a slope analysis and buildable area test. Canyon Rim lots are the usual example of steep ground.

  • These rules bite when someone builds or adds on, so they matter most if your buyer wants an addition.
  • Check with the city before relying on any relief option for single-family homes.
  • An owner who disputes a hazard on a lot can submit a site-specific geologic report to the county geologist.

Living near Mill Creek Canyon

The canyon is undeveloped national forest land in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest, just east of the East Mill Creek and Mount Olympus neighborhoods. It charges a $5 per vehicle fee on the way out, sells a $50 annual pass, and closes its upper half to vehicles from November 1 through July 1. Dogs may run off leash on odd-numbered days only.

If your house is near the canyon road, expect buyers to ask about weekend traffic and trail parking. A straight answer helps more than a glossy one.

Accessory dwelling units

Millcreek permits an accessory dwelling unit only on a lot with an owner-occupied home. The city records a notice on the title saying so, which means a buyer's title company will see it.

  • Internal and attached units can be short-term rentals with an ADU application and a Millcreek business license. Detached units cannot.
  • Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed in every ADU type, with an ADU compliance letter and a business license.
  • Each unit needs at least one off-street parking stall, and a separate utility meter is not allowed.
  • A detached unit needs an R-1 or A zone, a lot of at least 8,000 square feet, up to 1,000 square feet of floor area and a rear-yard location.

Since the rules turn on owner occupancy, an investor who buys the house can't assume the unit stays rentable. If you built a basement apartment without a permit, say so early.

Primary residence exemption and sales

Utah taxes a primary residence on 55 percent of market value, while a second home is taxed on all of it. To qualify, a household must use the home as its primary domicile for 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, and it can claim only one. The exemption does not follow a sale automatically, so a buyer who moves in files a new application with the county Board of Equalization by September 15. A late filing can cost the owner the exemption for that tax year.

A landlord renting to a full-time tenant can also claim it with a declaration signed by every owner. Starting January 1, 2027, a 2026 change requires owners to file Form TC-473A whenever ownership changes, including deed or trust transfers.

Property tax dates

Tax notices come from Salt Lake County by November 1. The bill can be paid without penalty through November 30, and anything outstanding is delinquent on December 1. A fall sale needs a quick conversation with the title company about how the current bill is divided at closing.

Preparing a Millcreek house for sale

Millcreek houses vary a lot, from flat western neighborhoods to foothill lots on Canyon Rim and Olympus Cove, so gather the facts that apply to yours. For a hillside lot, find any geologic or slope reports. For a house with an extra unit, find the ADU compliance letter and business license, or be ready to explain why there isn't one. For an older house, jot down the age of the roof, plumbing and wiring.

None of this has to be perfect before you reach out. A cash buyer works from the house as it is, and honest notes about its problems speed up the offer.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a Millcreek house for cash

Selling to us for cash means no mortgage underwriting, no appraisal gap and no staging. We price the house on its condition, and a title company runs the signing and files the deed with the county.

  1. Send the address and an honest description.
  2. We go over the details and name a price.
  3. Agree to it, and the title company drafts the closing paperwork.
  4. The deed is recorded and you are paid at closing.

This route tends to suit owners with an unpermitted unit, a hillside lot with a long repair list, or a stalled probate. Have your deed, any ADU letter or notice on the title, and the latest tax notice handy so the conversation goes quickly.

Frequently asked questions

When did Millcreek become a city?

The vote was November 3, 2015, and the city incorporated December 28, 2016. Before that it was a county township, from 2002.

Can I rent out an accessory dwelling unit in Millcreek?

Yes, provided an owner lives in the main home and the unit has a compliance letter. Short-term renting works for internal and attached units with an application and business license. Detached ones can't be short-term rentals.

What is the median home value in Millcreek?

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $627,200, a citywide number that can't price your own house.

When are property taxes due in Millcreek?

Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty on the current year's bill. After that, the balance turns delinquent on December 1.

Does the primary residence exemption transfer to a buyer?

No, the buyer has to apply again. The deadline is September 15, and filing late can forfeit that tax year's exemption.

Newer homes and what they mean for your sale

Newer construction usually brings fewer old-house surprises. A house with a tenant, a title tangle or unfinished work stands out in that setting, and financed buyers tend to skip it. The city kept annexing land as it grew, most recently the 933-acre Olympia development in 2022, so more new houses keep arriving to compete with yours.

Mail, City Hall and utilities

The city has no post office of its own. Mail runs through the Riverton Post Office at 12760 S 2080 W, so double-check the address on closing papers. City Hall is at 5355 West Herriman Main Street and keeps weekday hours from 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

Herriman City runs the water department. Other services come from separate providers, and you will move these accounts at closing.

Secondary water and your sale

Secondary water is a separate pressurized irrigation line for lawns and gardens, supplied by the Herriman City Water Department. It usually runs from early May to mid-October and then shuts down in stages.

To hook up, the owner has the sprinkler connection inspected, hands in a backflow test report if the yard also uses culinary water, and asks the city to set a secondary meter. The city installs the meter. A filter is smart because the water is filtered only to 200 microns.

If your yard still runs on culinary water, or the connection never passed inspection, expect questions from a buyer or inspector. The fix is simple, and a clean record spares you a delay.

Wildfire risk

Herriman is described as highly exposed to fire, with mountains, dry brush and open fields at its edges. A 2010 blaze that began during a National Guard exercise at nearby Camp Williams burned about 3,500 acres.

Utah's House Bill 48 of 2025 produced a statewide map rating buildings from 1 (lowest) to 8 (highest) for wildfire exposure. About 60,000 buildings statewide landed in the high-risk group, and those owners may face an annual state fee once the program starts. Type your address into wildfirerisk.utah.gov to see your score before a buyer does.

Basement and accessory apartment rules

Herriman permits an internal accessory dwelling unit, called an I-ADU, only inside a single-family home, and only one per lot. The owner has to live on the property, either in the main house or in the unit.

  • The unit needs its own exterior entrance with a hard-surface walkway.
  • The application review fee is $559, plus a building permit fee that varies with the remodeled area.
  • Plan review takes about 7 to 14 business days.
  • The owner signs a notarized affidavit, which is recorded with the County Recorder.
  • After a passed inspection and an approval letter, the owner needs a business license before renting.

Work done without a permit may need drywall and insulation pulled out for inspection. If your basement apartment was finished on the quiet, weigh that cost before you list.

Salt Lake County sets the calendar. Valuation notices are mailed July 22, and the Board of Equalization hears appeals from August 1 to September 15. Tax notices go out November 1, payment is due November 30, and unpaid current-year taxes turn delinquent on December 1.

A primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value under the 45% state exemption. Appeals cover market value only, so gather comparable sales or an appraisal before the window closes.

Recording the deed

The Salt Lake County Recorder files your deed for a flat $40, with up to ten legal descriptions included before extra charges apply. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number for each parcel. Your title company normally handles the filing right after closing.

Preparing a Herriman house for sale

Start with the paper trail. Find the permit and approval letter for any basement unit, the recorded affidavit if you have one, and the business license if you rented the space. Pull up your secondary water records so you can show the yard connection passed inspection.

Next, check your wildfire score and the age of the roof, then settle any water account balance so the buyer inherits a clean file. Walk the exterior and the yard the way an inspector would, noting anything a buyer might raise. Fixing a small thing now is cheaper than negotiating over it later. If a repair feels too big or too costly, that is the moment to consider a sale as-is, where the buyer takes the house in its present condition and you skip the project entirely.

  3. You say yes or no to the offer.

A half-finished I-ADU, a secondary water problem or a late tax bill can scare off a buyer who needs a loan. We buy the house as it stands, so those items get settled at closing and not before you list.

What a cash sale skips

You will not wait on a lender's appraisal, and you will not pay for repairs that a bank would demand. Showings, staging and open-house weekends are optional too. The title company still orders a search, collects any payoff for taxes or a mortgage and prepares the papers. If the house sits in a family trust or an estate, mention that when you first call.

Salt Lake County. Herriman sits in the southwest part of the county, so the county assessor, treasurer and recorder handle your parcel.

When are property taxes due in Herriman?

November 30 is the last day to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes are delinquent from December 1.

Can I rent out a basement apartment in Herriman?

Yes, if the home is a single-family house and the owner lives on the property. Herriman requires an I-ADU permit, a notarized affidavit recorded with the county, a passed final inspection and a business license before renting.

Which school district serves Herriman?

Jordan School District. Herriman has two high schools, Herriman High and Mountain Ridge High.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?

The flat recording fee is $40, plus $2 for each legal description beyond ten. The document needs a notary acknowledgment and the tax serial number of each parcel.

A young city on Utah Lake

Utah Lake and the Jordan River form its eastern side, the Lake Mountains foothills rise to the west, and it runs from Pelican Point on the lake up to Camp Williams, a U.S. Army facility.

It is also one of the newest cities on the Wasatch Front. Incorporation came on December 31, 1997, and the city status followed on May 31, 2001. The name comes from hot springs near the head of the Jordan River, where the Beck family ran a resort in 1884.

HOA paperwork and what buyers ask for

Plenty of homes in this city belong to an HOA, so begin with that paperwork before you list or rent. Read the community rules and ask for a payoff or status letter if assessments might be unpaid.

  • Pull together warranty papers, solar contracts and permit records, which buyers like to see.

Families who outgrow a starter house or relocate for work make up many of the sellers here, and a clean file of papers makes any sale go faster.

The Knolls Fire and wildfire questions

The Knolls Fire began in June 2020 south of the community on the shore of Utah Lake and burned about 15.6 square miles. About 3,100 homes in Saratoga Springs were evacuated. One home outside the city was destroyed and 12 others were damaged.

Road access is the lasting concern. A UDOT proposal for a Mountain View Corridor extension would give the southern part of the city a second evacuation route besides Redwood Road.

If your home is near the foothills or the lake, a buyer may ask about wildfire risk, insurance and escape routes. Answer plainly: what happened in 2020, how the roads work today, and what has changed since.

Roads: Redwood Road and the Mountain View Corridor

The agency expects it to pull up to 22,000 vehicles on weekdays off the Redwood Road corridor, and the plan includes two 12-foot shared-use trails.

Treat the extension as a proposal, not a promise, when you talk to buyers. A long-term road project may help a listing, but it should not be sold as something that is guaranteed.

School districts are changing

Saratoga Springs has been served by the Alpine School District, which covers Utah County from Orem northward. That district is being split. It is scheduled to cease to exist in July 2027, replaced by three new districts, Aspen Peaks, Timpanogos and Lake Mountain, and the last two were temporary names.

Westlake High School is in the city, along with elementary schools such as Harbor Point, Springside, Riverview, Thunder Ridge, Sage Hills, Harvest and Saratoga Shores, and middle schools Vista Heights and Lake Mountain. A payment not made by November 30 turns delinquent. The charge is 2.5 percent or $10, whichever is greater, on each parcel, and it drops to 1 percent or $10 for those who pay by January 31. If you are selling, your title company can split the year's tax between you and the buyer at closing.

Valuation notices arrive in the summer. Appeals go to the county board of equalization, located at 111 South University Avenue in Provo. File by September 15, or inside 45 days of your notice when that lands later.

Utah County's late appeal guidelines can accept a filing after the deadline, as late as March 31 of the next year, for a medical emergency, a death, a notice the county failed to send or a factual error in its records. Otherwise, file on time.

Recording fees in Utah County

Recording a document with the Utah County Recorder costs $40.00, with $2.00 more for each extra description or unit past ten. Certified copies are $5.00, and plain copies of recorded documents run $1.00 per page.

Card payments add a 2.65 percent processor fee with a $1.50 minimum, while electronic checks carry no processing fee. Your title company normally handles recording, so ask for a closing statement that itemizes these charges.

No bank approval stands between you and the closing date in a cash deal. Share the address, the shape the house is in and when you hope to move, and a written offer comes back. Accept it and a title company takes over: the deed gets recorded at the county and your proceeds are paid out.

It tends to fit people relocating on short notice, houses in rough shape, rentals and inherited homes. Set the number beside a listing's likely result after agent fees, repairs and months of carrying costs. Saying no carries no penalty.

For an HOA home, line up the status letter early. For a house near the lake or foothills, be ready to talk about the fire history. Having those answers up front keeps the process short.

If taxes are still owed at sale

Being behind on property tax does not stop a sale. The title company lists the overdue amount as a payoff and pays it out of your proceeds at closing, next to any mortgage. Request a current payoff figure from the county so the settlement statement holds no surprises.

Unpaid HOA dues work the same way. Get the balance in writing, pass it along and it is cleared as the deed transfers.

Listing is a fine route for a spotless house in a well-run HOA when you are not in a hurry. A cash sale fits a seller short on time, or a house that would need money spent on it before it could be shown.

Utah County. County offices assess and bill the homes, and valuation appeals are heard by the county board of equalization.

When did Saratoga Springs become a city?

Incorporation was December 31, 1997, and the city status followed on May 31, 2001.

A June 2020 wildfire that started south of the community on the Utah Lake shore. About 3,100 homes were evacuated, one home outside the city was destroyed and 12 were damaged.

September 15, or 45 days after your notice if that falls later. A few late filings are accepted until March 31 of the following year.

Yes. Ask your HOA for a payoff or status letter first, because unpaid assessments get cleared at closing.

Logan is the Cache County seat, about 47 miles north of Ogden and 82 miles north of Salt Lake City, on the Logan River at the foot of the Bear River Mountains. Streets on the east side climb across benches of old Lake Bonneville sediment, while the flat west side is closer to farmland and marsh. Winter and your house

Logan has warm, usually dry summers and cold winters with moderate snow: about 18.97 inches of precipitation and 61.5 inches of snow a year. The record low is minus 25 degrees. Roofs carry snow for months, and pipes in a vacant house can freeze. If you cannot heat or check on an empty house through the cold months, closing before winter may be the safer plan.

Utah State University and the rental market

Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are the largest employers, and the main campus covers roughly 600 acres at the mouth of Logan Canyon. Other employers include ICON Health and Fitness, Campbell Scientific, Logan Regional Hospital, JBS USA, Schreiber Foods and Thermo Fisher Scientific. A seller with a rental near campus should think about the academic calendar when choosing a closing date.

Logan City School District runs eight public schools, and Cache County School District serves some Logan neighborhoods too, so confirm the boundary for your address. Connect Transit runs 15 zero-fare routes through Logan, North Logan and River Heights.

Landlord licensing and occupancy rules

Every owner of a rental unit must hold a Logan landlord business license, and each ownership entity such as an LLC, trust or corporation needs its own. The exception covers an owner-occupied home rented only during a hospital or nursing home stay, or a temporary absence of three years or less.

Cache County property tax

The calendar is simple. Valuation notices go out in July, appeals run from August to September, tax notices arrive in October and payment is due November 30. Current-year taxes turn delinquent in December. Prior-year delinquent taxes are posted in January, and the Treasurer collects them or notifies new owners by the end of that month.

Utah takes 45 percent off the market value of a primary home, with a 183 consecutive day residency test. A buyer files Form TC-473A by September 15 after the sale, and counties cannot accept late filings.

Recording and taxes owed

The Cache County Recorder files the deed, and a state change added $5 to county recording fees, so ask for the current total. If you owe taxes when you sell, the title company pays them from your proceeds at closing, so there is nothing separate for you to chase down.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Logan houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a cash sale works in Logan

A Logan cash sale is an ordinary closing with no mortgage lender in the middle. The buyer reviews the property, makes an offer, and a title company handles liens, taxes and the deed.

  • Describe the house and any tenants or lease dates.
  • Review the offer and the closing date.
  • Close with a title company and have the deed recorded in Cache County.

Rental owners with a lease running to a set date, heirs managing from afar and owners who would rather not pay for repairs most often choose this route. A buyer who takes the house with tenants in place can ask for the lease and the occupancy disclosure form.

What a cash sale skips

You skip the lender's appraisal, the bank's repair list, the staging and the open houses. With a student rental, you also skip the awkward task of showing rooms to strangers while tenants live there. The title work stays, and you decide the closing date, whether you want it soon or after the lease ends.

Selling a Logan house with tenants

A lease does not end because the owner decides to sell. Read it first and note the end date, the deposit and any renewal rights. A cash buyer can take the house with tenants in place, which spares you from asking students to leave early or from timing a closing around the school year. If you want the house empty, a cash buyer is also more flexible about waiting until the lease ends.

Hand the title company a copy of each lease so the deposit can be credited to the buyer at closing. Tell tenants in writing when the sale is happening and whom to contact afterward, so rent goes to the right place.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to gather before you sell

Pull together the deed or trust papers, the landlord license, the lease and the zoning occupancy disclosure form, your latest tax notice and any code notices. Add notes on the roof age and the heating system, since winter wear is the first thing a buyer asks about. A short folder of papers shortens the title work and answers an investor's first round of questions before they are asked.

Selling with taxes owed

An open tax bill is not a roadblock. Ask the Cache County Treasurer for the payoff and give it to the title officer. The amount is subtracted from your check, and the year is divided between you and the buyer so each of you carries only your own months.

History in short

Brigham Young sent settlers in 1859, and Logan was incorporated on January 17, 1866. The Cache County Historic Courthouse went up in 1883, the Logan Utah Temple was completed in 1884, and the Agricultural College of Utah, now Utah State University, opened on September 2, 1890. Cache County leads Utah in dairy products and is a major producer of hay, alfalfa and grain.

Frequently asked questions

How many people live in Logan, Utah?

The estimate is 55,576 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 52,778.

Do I need a landlord license to rent a house in Logan?

Yes. Logan requires a landlord business license for every owner of a rental unit, with a narrow exception for a temporary absence of three years or less. Call 435-716-9230 for fees and renewal.

When are Cache County property taxes due?

By November 30. The Treasurer mails tax notices in October, and unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent in December.

How many unrelated people can live in a Logan house?

Generally three unrelated people, or one family plus one more person. Campus Residential zones allow up to six, with no more than two per bedroom.

What is the largest employer in Logan?

Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are the largest employers in Logan.

Murray in brief

Murray occupies the core of the Salt Lake Valley and touches Taylorsville, Holladay, South Salt Lake, Millcreek and West Jordan. The Jordan River marks its western edge, and Big and Little Cottonwood Creeks both run through town to reach it. The 2020 count was 50,637 people, up from 46,746 in 2010.

Nearly two thirds of homes are lived in by their owners, which makes Murray a more owner-heavy market than some of its neighbors. A short summary of the housing picture follows.

From smelter town to medical center

Settlers arrived in 1848, and the city incorporated on January 3, 1903. The smelting era ran from about 1870 until ASARCO's lead smelter closed in 1949, and the stacks came down in 2000. Intermountain Healthcare bought the site, and Intermountain Medical Center, which replaced Cottonwood Hospital in 2007, is now one of the city's largest employers.

Retail followed in the 1970s with Fashion Place Mall and a State Street lined with car dealerships. For a seller, the takeaway is simple: Murray is a long-established city with a large hospital campus nearby and a steady base of owner-occupied homes.

City-run utilities

Murray runs its own police, fire, power, water, sewer, library and parks departments. In many areas it supplies power, water, sewer, garbage and stormwater service, though other providers cover properties where the city has no infrastructure. Murray City Power, publicly owned since 1913, serves about 18,000 customers.

  • Call the utility billing office at (801) 264-2626 to ask how a final reading and a transfer of service work for your address.
  • The office is at 10 East 4800 South, Suite 160.

Transit and highways

Three light rail stations serve Murray: Murray North, Murray Central and Fashion Place West, on the Blue and Red lines. Murray Central is also where FrontRunner commuter rail, which opened in December 2012, meets TRAX, and it is the only such connection outside Salt Lake City. Interstate 15 and Interstate 215 both cross the city, and mean travel time to work is 20.7 minutes.

If your house is a short walk from a station, put that in the listing.

Murray neighborhoods

Murray has its own school district, though some addresses fall in Granite School District instead, so the school an address belongs to depends on the street. Confirm the zone before quoting it to a buyer.

  • Bergertown, south of 4800 South along Little Cottonwood Creek, began as a Swiss immigrant enclave.
  • The Murray Downtown Historic District follows State Street.
  • Murray City Park covers 22 acres with a baseball stadium and an amphitheatre.
  • The Jordan River Parkway trail runs along the western edge.

Rental houses and accessory units

The city treats a residential rental as a business, so the owner needs a current Murray business license. One license covers every rental held by the same legal entity, and hiring a property manager does not replace it.

A license can't be moved between owners or addresses. A buyer who inherits your tenants must apply for a new one. Running a rental without a license, or after one lapses, brings a penalty of 100 percent of the past-due fees under City Code 5.04.280. Renewal notices go out on the first of the month the license expires, and a postmark does not prove timely receipt.

Each lot may have one accessory dwelling unit, and the owner must live in the main house or the unit. A detached unit needs a lot of at least 10,000 square feet, a height of 20 feet or less and a single story, and it can't sit in the front yard. Renting an ADU for stays shorter than 30 days is prohibited. Before the application is accepted, an affidavit on occupancy and short-term rental terms must be recorded with the Salt Lake County Recorder.

Fault lines and creeks

Murray shares the valley's earthquake exposure. The Wasatch Fault and soft lake sediments shape building risk across the Wasatch Front. The Salt Lake City segment last ruptured 1,200 to 1,300 years ago, and the chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years is put at 57 percent.

Expect an inspector to flag chimney bracing, an unstrapped water heater and foundation cracks. If the lot is near Big or Little Cottonwood Creek, ask the county for flood zone information.

Property tax calendar

Salt Lake County sets the dates for every Murray property. Value is measured as of January 1. Valuation notices go out in July and August, with a 45 day Board of Equalization window counted from the original mailing. Tax notices are mailed by November 1, the penalty-free payment deadline is November 30, and delinquency starts December 1.

Recording a deed in Salt Lake County

The county's 2024 recording requirements call for white 8.5 by 11 inch paper, a legible caption on the first page, the grantee's name and mailing address, and a legal description. The grantor's name must read the same on the title, the document, the notary acknowledgment and the signature. A flat $40 recording fee was listed, so confirm the amount before you sign. A title company normally handles all this for a sale.

If you are selling a rental in Murray

Landlords have a few extra items to clear. Confirm the Murray business license is current, since a lapse carries a penalty on past-due fees. Collect the lease and rent roll for the buyer. If a detached unit was added, locate the recorded affidavit, because the buyer's title company will see it on file with the county. Where a tenant is staying, agree early on how and when the buyer takes over the lease so closing does not stall.

Selling a Murray house for cash

A cash sale still closes through a title company in the usual way, minus the buyer's lender. We look at the house as it stands, make an offer, and the title company takes care of the signing and the county recording.

  1. Tell us about the house, including tenants or an ADU if there is one.
  2. We review it and quote a price.
  3. You accept or decline, with no obligation either way.
  4. If you accept, the title company sets the closing.

Murray owners most often reach out about inherited homes, rentals with tenants and houses that need work. Bring the rental license if you have one, any ADU affidavit and the newest tax notice, and the process moves faster.

Frequently asked questions

What school district is Murray, Utah in?

Most of the city is in Murray City School District. Granite School District serves some addresses, so check the district for a specific one.

Who supplies electricity in Murray?

Murray City Power, a municipal utility created in 1913, serves about 18,000 customers. The city also supplies water, sewer and garbage service in many areas.

Do I need a business license to rent out a Murray house?

Yes. One license covers all rentals owned by the same legal entity, and it can't be transferred to a buyer.

Can I rent an accessory dwelling unit short term in Murray?

No. Rentals shorter than 30 days are prohibited in an ADU, and the owner must live on the property.

When are Murray property taxes due?

Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1.

Why the county line matters in Draper

About 20 miles south of Salt Lake City, Draper straddles two counties, Salt Lake and Utah. The city covers roughly 30 square miles at an elevation of 4,751 feet, right where the Salt Lake Valley narrows into Utah Valley at the Point of the Mountain.

That line decides who assesses your house, who mails the bill and where the deed gets filed. Schools split along it as well, with Canyons on the Salt Lake County side and Alpine on the Utah County side. Look at the parcel number on your tax notice first. Neighbors a few blocks apart can answer to different offices, calendars and school boundaries.

Draper had 51,017 residents in 2020, up from 7,257 in 1990. Many neighborhoods were built in that window, so houses range from old farm lots to subdivisions less than a generation old. The median home value is $784,800, median gross rent is $1,894, and 68.6% of homes are owner-occupied. That leaves roughly 31% rented, so if you are selling a rental, the tenant situation matters as much as the building.

Wildfire risk and your sale

Foothill homes are most exposed. The city council adopted Ordinance 1695 in December 2025, which adds a Wildland Urban Interface Area to city code. Boundaries and rules are not spelled out in the public notice, so request the full ordinance from the city if your lot backs onto open hillside.

A separate state program adds another layer. Utah House Bill 48 of 2025 led the state forestry division to publish a wildfire risk map scoring each building from 1 to 8. A building that scores 7 or higher and sits within 250 meters of at least two other buildings falls inside the high-risk boundary, and its owner may owe the state an annual fee once the program starts, which the state expected later in 2026.

  • Enter your address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov ahead of listing or answering an offer.
  • Save a printed score to hand over with the contract.
  • Ask city planning whether the lot lies in the new interface area.

Short-term rentals and accessory units

Two approvals are required to host short stays in Draper: a business license and a short-term rental permit. Short term means under 30 consecutive days, with a two-night minimum, and the permit renews yearly. A day of unpermitted hosting is a separate violation each time.

Accessory dwelling units have separate limits.

  • A detached ADU needs a residential lot of at least 12,000 square feet.
  • An internal ADU generally needs a residential lot over 6,000 square feet on a qualifying street, and the city has mapped areas where internal units are banned.
  • The owner must live in the main dwelling for both types.
  • ADU rentals must run at least 30 consecutive days, and each needs one extra on-site parking space.

Basement apartments built without permits are a frequent problem. Owners who skipped the February 1, 2022 application window face immediate enforcement, and a buyer relying on a loan may balk. Draper's planning office answers questions at (801) 576-6399.

Filing costs little. Salt Lake County takes a flat $40 per recording, and Utah County's standard fee is the same $40 per document. In Salt Lake County the deed also needs a notary acknowledgment, the grantee's address and the tax serial number. The title company works out the closing date with you.

Papers to gather first

Begin with the parcel number and latest tax notice, which show the county that applies. Add any ADU permit or application receipt, your short-term rental permit and renewal date, the wildfire score printout and your loan payoff figures, plus the lease if a tenant lives there.

Wildfire paperwork deserves its own line in that folder. The state map can change how a buyer sees a foothill house, and the annual fee tied to high-risk buildings is not yet in place. Showing the score upfront, along with what you know about defensible space around the house, keeps the conversation factual.

Giving the title officer this folder at the outset cuts the back-and-forth that drags out many closings. A buyer also sees what the house may and may not be used for before signing.

What slows a Draper sale?

Five problems recur.

  • A hillside lot with a high state wildfire score.
  • An older basement unit with no ADU permit.
  • A short-term rental permit that lapsed after its annual renewal.
  • A tenant in place on a rental.
  • Confusion over whether the parcel is billed by Salt Lake County or Utah County.

Order matters here: sort out the county first, then permits, then the wildfire score. Each answer shapes the next conversation with a buyer or the title office.

Rentals add another wrinkle. With roughly 31% of occupied homes not owner-occupied, many Draper buyers expect to see lease terms, so have the dates, rent and deposit ready if a tenant is in the house.

All can be solved, yet each adds steps to a conventional listing. Selling directly lets the house go as it stands, with paperwork sorted at the title company.

Getting around and nearby employers

Part of the Silicon Slopes tech corridor, Draper reports more than 1,000 businesses. Interstate 15 crosses town, TRAX Blue Line trains stop at Draper Town Center and Kimballs Lane, and FrontRunner has a station here. Two airports, Salt Lake International and Provo Municipal, are about 30 minutes away. Tech workers and rail commuters often ask how far a house is from the stations.

Is Draper in Salt Lake County or Utah County?

Both. Which county handles your bill and deed depends on the parcel, and the number on your tax notice tells you.

When are Draper property taxes due?

In both counties the deadline is November 30, shifting to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday.

Do I need a permit to rent my Draper house short term?

Yes. You need a business license and a short-term rental permit, renewed annually. Every day without both is its own violation.

Can I sell a Draper house that has an unpermitted basement apartment?

Yes, though buyers will ask. An ADU permit comes before any rental, and the owner must live in the main dwelling. Cash buyers can take the house as is. Financed buyers may want the permit settled first.

How do I check wildfire risk for a Draper address?

Type it in at wildfirerisk.utah.gov to get a score from 1 to 8. A building scoring 7 or higher near other buildings counts as high risk.

Spanish Fork at a glance

Spanish Fork is a Utah County city at the crossing of Interstate 15 and US-6. Salt Lake City lies about 50 miles north and Provo about 10 miles north, with the Wasatch Range to the east and Utah Lake to the northwest. Springville is about 4 miles northeast, Salem about 4.5 miles south and Payson about 6 miles southwest. The elevation is near 4,666 feet.

Property tax here is a Utah County matter, and the assessor, treasurer and recorder all work from Provo. Nebo School District operates the public schools.

Population, 2020 count42,602

Owners live in most homes, and households run large. Treat the median as a rough survey number, since a given house can price far from it. Permits issued in 2022 covered 810 new homes, 190 single-family and 620 multi-family, so an older property is competing against fresh construction.

Roads, rail and schools

I-15 runs north to Salt Lake City and south toward Las Vegas. US-6 climbs east through Spanish Fork Canyon toward Denver. SR-51 and Main Street bring in more traffic, and Union Pacific trains pass through town. Main Street and US-6 carry about 60,000 vehicles per day, and the average commute is 20.0 minutes.

Families will ask about schools. Spanish Fork High and Maple Mountain High are the main high schools, Spanish Fork Junior High and Diamond Fork Middle cover the middle grades, Landmark High is an alternative school and American Leadership Academy is a K to 12 charter. Fifteen of the district's roughly 50 schools are inside the city limits. Ask the district about the school for a specific address before you name one to a buyer.

Commuters also care about road access. A house close to the I-15 and US-6 junction is easy to reach from the rest of the county, which is worth saying in a description.

Snow, water and utilities

Winter and water are the two local quirks. The city averages 66 inches of snow and 21.88 inches of rain a year, at a mean temperature of 52.1 degrees Fahrenheit. Roof and furnace condition therefore weigh heavily with buyers.

Two separate systems deliver water. One supplies indoor drinking water, and a pressurized irrigation network feeds lawns and landscaping. With a yard, expect buyers to ask if the irrigation hookup works and what it costs in season.

The city also operates Spanish Fork Power & Light, where the average monthly residential bill is $77.11, and Spanish Fork Community Network for fiber, phone and cable. Natural gas comes from Dominion Energy.

Accessory dwelling units

The city permits a single ADU for each single-family home, provided the owner lives on site.

  • The lot must be at least 6,000 square feet, and ADUs are barred in A-E, R-4, R-5 and R-O zones.
  • Parking: three off-street spaces for an internal ADU and four for a detached ADU.
  • Each ADU must register every year with Community Development through CitizenServe for a $60 fee.
  • Impact fees and a separate electric meter are not required.

Registration renews yearly, so show a buyer the current paperwork for any unit you advertise. Reach the Building Division at 801-804-4540.

Due dates and penalties

The county sends the tax notice in the second half of October, and payment is due by November 30. A residence you live in is 45% exempt, which makes 55% of its market value taxable.

Delinquent amounts from earlier years are absent from the current bill, so request a payoff figure from the Treasurer before closing. Visit 100 East Center Street, Suite 1200 in Provo, or call 801-851-8255. Online payment is available. The Recorder, in Suite 1300, answers at 801-851-8179.

How to appeal your valuation

Your valuation notice comes first, and it explains how to appeal to the Board of Equalization. File by September 15, or 45 days after the notice was mailed when that is later. For a value you believe is too high, line up comparable sales and repair quotes before you submit.

How a cash sale works in Spanish Fork

Showing proof of funds takes the place of loan approval, which leaves title work as the main clock. You describe the house and when you want to move, look over the offer and sign a purchase agreement.

A title or escrow company handles settlement, the deed goes to the Utah County Recorder and taxes are prorated up to the closing date. Collect roof and furnace dates, any ADU registration, irrigation details and a recent utility bill beforehand. For an inherited house or a job move, closing on your own schedule can be worth more than a slightly higher price.

Selling a house that has an ADU

An ADU can raise value or raise questions. Buyers ask if the unit is registered, if it satisfies the lot and parking rules and if someone rents it now. Keep the registration papers handy, plus the lease and rent history when there is a tenant.

A unit that was never registered leaves two options. Bring it into compliance before listing, or sell as is to a cash buyer who handles the unit later. The right pick depends on the cost of compliance and your preferred closing speed.

Selling when taxes are owed

Old taxes will not block a sale. The title company lists them as a payoff on the closing statement and deducts them from your proceeds. Phone the Treasurer in Provo for the number, because earlier-year balances are not on this year's bill, and pass it to the title company soon.

This year's tax is divided at the closing date. When November 30 is near, decide who writes the check and record that choice in the purchase agreement.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps from first call to closing

  1. Send us the address, a description of the house and your target move date.
  2. We look at the house and return a written offer.
  3. On acceptance, you sign a purchase agreement and a title company opens the file.
  4. Title staff verify ownership, taxes and liens.
  5. You sign the closing papers, the deed is recorded in Provo and your proceeds are released.

No lender sits in the middle, so the date you pick and the title work set the pace.

Snags sellers run into

  • An ADU that was never registered, or one that violates lot rules.
  • Irrigation or yard problems that a buyer finds on a walkthrough.

Riverton at a glance

Riverton is a Salt Lake County suburb tucked into the valley's southwest corner, roughly 20 miles from downtown Salt Lake City. It covers 12.58 square miles at 4,439 feet. South Jordan lies to the north, Draper to the east, Bluffdale to the south and Herriman to the west. Tax bills, appeals and deed recording are all handled by county offices downtown.

Owners occupy 84.9% of homes, so most sellers are parting with a family house on a block of other owners. Population reached 45,285 in 2020, a 16.9% gain over 2010's 38,753, and is estimated at 47,395 for July 1, 2025.

From farm town to suburb

Riverton began as a farming community in the mid-1850s and was first called Gardnerville. Alfalfa, wheat, sugar beets, tomatoes, poultry, sheep and dairy kept the town busy into the twentieth century. The city incorporated in the late 1940s, a 1996 annexation nearly doubled its size, and Herriman's incorporation in 2000 fixed the western boundary.

Growth came in pieces, which means a house's age depends on where in town it stands.

Neighborhoods

Several named areas began as specific developments.

  • Tithing Yard Hill is a residential planned development named for a former LDS tithing storage site.
  • Foothills was annexed in the 1980s, de-annexed after the developer's bankruptcy, and re-annexed in 1996.

Intermountain Riverton Hospital, which opened in November 2009 with a 24-hour emergency department, sits inside the city limits.

The main roads are Bangerter Highway, the Mountain View Corridor and Redwood Road, and drivers reach Interstate 15 through 12300 South or Bangerter Highway. Bangerter Highway (SR-154) curves north into Riverton and crosses 13400 South, 12600 South and 11400 South. The 12600 South interchange opened on May 19, 2022.

Transit is limited. UTA Route 126, which began in April 2025, runs hourly along 12600 South. Riverton workers average 24.8 minutes to get to work, so mention commute routes in a listing. Accessory dwellings and short-term rentals

The city handles accessory dwellings through an application and an owner-occupancy affidavit filed at City Hall. Short-term rentals go through a conditional use permit and an occupancy declaration. Confirm the city's current ordinance before you describe an apartment in a Riverton house as legal.

  • Submit online, mail form BE01, or go to 2001 South State Street, Suite N3-300, Salt Lake City.
  • Back the appeal with evidence: at least three comparable sales within the year before January 1, a signed settlement statement or a fee appraisal.
  • Only total market value can be contested, not land or improvements alone.
  • The Board adjusts the valuation, never the tax itself.

A hearing officer weighs the evidence, with county review of appeals around October 1 unless the State Tax Commission extends it. If you lose, you have 30 days to take it to the Utah State Tax Commission. Call the appeals office at 385-468-7200 with questions.

Property tax due date

Payment is due November 30 even when an appeal is still pending, so pay first and let any adjustment follow. Whatever is still owed at closing comes out of your proceeds through the title company.

Running about 240 miles, the Wasatch Fault has a Salt Lake City segment that last broke some 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. On any one central segment, quakes of magnitude 7 or larger come every 900 to 1,300 years. On March 18, 2020, a magnitude 5.7 quake just north of Magna did moderate damage.

Annual precipitation is 15.76 inches, with winter snow and summers that sometimes pass 100 degrees. Inspectors may check foundations and chimneys, and an as-is seller is not obliged to fix what they find.

Preparing a family home for sale

Most Riverton sellers have lived in the house for years and know its quirks, so put them on paper. Note how old the roof, furnace and water heater are, any basement finishing done without a permit, and repairs you keep postponing. Then pull out the deed, the newest tax notice and your valuation notice if you kept it.

Perfect records are not required. We work from the house as it stands, and clear notes let us give a realistic offer early. If the house has a finished basement, say whether it was permitted. If it has a separate entrance or a kitchen down there, mention that too, since the city's rules on accessory dwellings and owner occupancy will apply to anyone who plans to rent it out. Telling us now means no surprises for either side later.

What happens at closing

Once you agree to a price, the closing company verifies ownership and searches for liens or unpaid tax. You sign, the deed is filed with the county recorder, and payment follows. Nobody has to approve a mortgage or order an appraisal, the two steps that most often hold up an ordinary sale. Need a certain closing date? Say so at the outset and we will plan around it.

Common situations include an inherited family home, a house with a basement apartment that lacks paperwork, or a move on a short deadline.

Between August 1 and September 15, or 45 days from the notice if that is later.

Bountiful's layout and what it means for a house

Bountiful sits in Davis County on the slope between the Wasatch Range and the Great Salt Lake flats, at about 4,771 feet and roughly 13 square miles. The 2020 count was 45,762 people in 15,427 households and 15,945 housing units. Few lots are left to build on, so most sales are resales of houses with decades of wear.

Old downtown is at the foot of the mountains, homes climb the eastern benches, and the west side is flat and runs toward the lake. Most land east of the city is Forest Service ground, which is why the hillside streets stop where public land starts. North Salt Lake, Woods Cross, West Bountiful and Centerville are the neighbors. A bench-street lot and a west-side lot are very different properties, and buyers know it.

Roofs, snow and older masonry

A typical year brings about 23 inches of precipitation and about 59 inches of snow, with a record high of 104 degrees and a record low of minus 9. Roofs, furnaces and cooling systems all get used. Inspectors in a snow climate usually look first at the roof surface, attic insulation and gutters, so expect questions if those have not been touched in years.

The Wasatch Fault follows the base of the range, and more than 85 percent of Utahns live in the earthquake zone along the Wasatch Front. Unreinforced masonry is a particular worry. If your Bountiful house is older brick, a buyer may ask about chimneys, foundations and any retrofit.

  • Roof age and snow load on the east benches
  • Brick chimneys and masonry walls
  • Drainage on steep hillside lots
  • Furnace and water heater age

Getting around

Interstate 15 is the main road, and FrontRunner commuter rail has served the city since April 2008. Legacy Parkway opened on September 13, 2008, to ease pressure on the interstate. The narrow gap into Salt Lake County still slows rush hour, which is worth a line for buyers who commute south. Houses a short drive from the Mueller Park Canyon trailheads tend to draw extra attention from hikers.

Closing out electric and water service

Bountiful City runs its own electric department and also handles utility billing. The power office is at 198 South 200 West. Utility billing is 801-298-6100, and the 24-hour outage line is 801-298-6072. City Hall is at 795 South Main Street.

A live utility representative has to set up or end service, which rules out an online form. Call ahead of closing. With the sale date fixed, the last meter reading and final bill are easier to settle.

  • Call 801-298-6100 to schedule the end of service.

  • Keep a copy of the closed account.

How Bountiful property tax is billed and paid

Davis County bills Bountiful property tax, and payment is due each year on November 30. When November 30 falls on a weekend, the deadline rolls to the next business day. Pay at the treasurer's office, 61 South Main Street, Room 105, Farmington, or call 801-451-3243.

Utah Code 59-2-103 cuts residential value by 45 percent, so 55 percent is taxed. Land counts toward that cut only up to one acre for each residential unit.

If a lender escrows your taxes, it may pay through a third-party service, and that can delay posting by several days. Check the account before you list.

Your Notice of Property Market Valuation carries the appeal deadline. Submit the Board of Equalization form to the Davis County Controller, one application for each parcel, giving your own view of value as of January 1. Questions go to 801-451-3323.

Acceptable proof includes a recent closing statement, a full appraisal, three or more comparable sales within one mile, an income statement, a documented factual error, or evidence of damage. The appeal covers this year's market value only. The tax rate cannot be challenged.

Selling mid-year does not end an appeal, because both it and the bill follow the property. Let the buyer's side know what is pending so any refund is routed properly.

Selling for cash avoids the lender appraisal and repair haggling that tend to follow a listing, and the date is yours to pick. Four steps cover it.

  1. Describe the house honestly, tenants, liens and repairs included.
  2. Take the buyer's offer or turn it down.
  3. Escrow opens, title is searched and payoffs are requested.
  4. You sign, escrow divides the year's tax between you and the buyer, and the money is yours.

Bring the latest tax notice and any loan payoff details. If a tenant lives there, bring the lease so move-out terms can be written into the contract.

Papers to have ready

Before the title company opens escrow, pull together the newest Davis County tax notice, proof that any lender-escrowed tax was posted, the mortgage payoff figure and the age of the roof, furnace and water heater. Older Bountiful houses draw questions on all three systems, and a written answer beats a guess. Add the valuation notice if an appeal is pending, and the lease if the house is rented.

Sellers of inherited houses should also gather whatever shows who may sign. The title company will want every signature collected before it sets a date, and that step usually decides how long the sale takes.

What Bountiful sellers usually run into

People who sell fast in Bountiful tend to own an older house, a hillside lot, or a place they must move quickly.

  • Older homes that need roof, electrical or plumbing work before a retail buyer can get a loan
  • Inherited houses where several relatives must agree before anyone signs
  • Rentals with tenants in place and a lease that runs past the sale date
  • Overdue repairs that make a traditional listing hard to price

If you are unsure which bucket your house falls in, a quick walk-through with a contractor or inspector gives you a written list of what a retail buyer would ask you to fix. Compare that list against the offer you would get as-is before you spend money on repairs.

The resale pool is wide because the city is close to Salt Lake City and on the FrontRunner line. That helps a well-kept house. It does less for a property that needs work, which is where an as-is sale fits.

Your primary residence already gets the 45 percent reduction. If the market value on your notice seems too high, appeal to the Board of Equalization through the Davis County Controller before the printed date.

Forty minutes southwest of Salt Lake City, on the western slope of the Oquirrh Mountains at 4,915 feet, Tooele is the seat of Tooele County. Tooele keeps growing. The city counted 35,742 people in 2020 and is estimated at 42,270 on July 1, 2025. Older neighborhoods such as New Town, built for smelter workers, sit beside newer areas that have added thousands of residents since 2020.

Getting to Salt Lake City

Most trips to the capital use State Route 36 to Interstate 80, and that junction jams. It is the first exit for westbound drivers on I-80, and a storm or crash can back it up for hours.

State Route 179, the Midvalley Highway, opened October 30, 2021. About 4.5 miles long, it ties SR-138 to I-80, so people heading to Erda and Grantsville can skip SR-36. UDOT expected it to cut traffic at the I-80 and SR-36 interchange by 15% to 20%, or about 6,000 to 8,000 vehicles a day. It opened with a single lane each way, and more lanes are planned with no date set.

The county grew 25% between 2010 and 2020, fifth-fastest among Utah counties and well above the 18.4% statewide rate. If you commute, state the drive time in your listing, because buyers will ask.

Jobs nearby

Work here spans mining, industry, defense and government. Kennecott Utah Copper operates the Bingham Canyon Mine on the far side of the Oquirrh Mountains, while EnergySolutions and US Magnesium work west of the valley. Former Army buildings at Tooele Industrial Depot now house manufacturing, warehousing and offices. Federal, state and county agencies employ a good share of residents too.

Schools

The county school district has its headquarters in Tooele, and 8 of its 16 elementary schools, 2 of 3 junior highs and 2 of 5 high schools (Tooele High and Blue Peak) are inside the city. The city is also home to a regional Utah State University campus and the Tooele Applied Technology College. Families wanting alternatives can look at Saint Marguerite Catholic School and Scholar Academy Charter School.

Due dates and penalties

  • Sales of comparable properties before January 1 that sold for less than your value.
  • Your own purchase before January 1, shown with a settlement statement. Short sales, bank-owned and foreclosure sales generally need an appraisal.
  • An appraisal with an effective date within the year.
  • A written statement of a factual error, such as wrong square footage or garage type.

You can look at your property card in person Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Card details are available in person only.

Selling an inherited house

Many sales here come from estates. As an heir, start with who has the legal authority to sign, and collect the papers that show it. Walk the house and decide what stays, what goes and who gets it. Then ask the county for the current tax status so nothing surprises you at the closing table.

A house left empty may have put-off maintenance, an aging roof or furnace, or leftover belongings no one wants. A cash buyer prices all of that in, so clearing out, fixing and staging are not required before you hear a number.

Around older streets like New Town, inspectors study roofs, windows, plumbing and wiring. In newer subdivisions the focus shifts to drainage and finishes. A buyer with a mortgage will probably send a repair request after the inspection, and selling as is spares you that negotiation.

In any sale, three kinds of records help: dates for the roof and furnace, permit papers for any addition and receipts for recent work. Together they show a buyer that someone looked after the house, and they save time during the title and offer stages. Keep them in one folder.

Without a lender, the timeline follows the title work and the date you pick, which can be soon or several weeks out if you need time to move. If you have already lined up a new place, say so, and a closing date can be built around your keys and your moving truck.

What a cash sale offers a Tooele seller

People sell for many reasons, and a cash sale fits when you would rather not repair the house, handle showings or wait on a loan. We buy Tooele houses as is, whether they need maintenance, have tenants or belong to an unsettled estate. You get an offer and choose whether to take it.

When must I appeal a Tooele County valuation?

Within 45 days of receiving the notice, or by September 15. The county mails notices at the end of July.

How far is Tooele from Salt Lake City?

Roughly 40 minutes southwest. Drivers mostly take State Route 36 to Interstate 80, and the Midvalley Highway (SR-179), opened in 2021, eases pressure on that interchange.

January's mean daily high is 37 degrees Fahrenheit, July's is 94, and the record low is minus 26. Roy gets about 18.4 inches of precipitation a year, mostly in April or May.

Repeated freezing and thawing cracks concrete, strains exposed pipes and wears out asphalt shingles early. An aging roof is among the usual reasons a traditional buyer asks for a lower price.

Schools and parks

Weber School District covers Roy entirely. Seven elementary schools, three junior highs and two high schools serve the city. Newer ones such as Haven Bay Elementary, Mountain View Junior High and West Field High may be missing from older lists, so ask the district which school an address feeds.

The Roy City Recreation Complex on the high school campus has a pool, basketball courts, a weight room, racquetball courts and an indoor track, and the Roy Aquatic Center is an outdoor complex. Each August, Roy Days brings a parade, a car show and fireworks to Roy West Park.

Permits for repairs before you sell

A permit is required for many Roy repairs and additions, filed online through the My City Inspector portal. A plan set for a one or two family dwelling must include a site plan, footing and foundation plan, floor plans, elevations, insulation R-values and energy compliance documents. State law aims for initial plan review within 14 business days of acceptance. Phone the Building Official about fees and exempt projects first.

Roy sales often stall on unpermitted work, since a lender or inspector may ask about a finished basement or converted garage. Selling as-is spares you from permitting and finishing jobs you would rather not fund.

Weber County property tax

Weber County sends Roy's tax bills, payable by November 30 unless that day lands on a weekend or holiday. Value is set as of January 1, and a primary residence gets a 45 percent exemption on the buildings and up to one acre of land.

Valuation notices typically arrive around the end of July or start of August. Appeal by September 15, or within 45 days of the notice if that is later. The county accepts late appeals only for severe circumstances: a death in the family, a dire medical emergency or a factual error in the property description.

Delinquent taxes and penalties

  • A bill unpaid on December 1 is delinquent.
  • Clear it in full by January 31 and the penalty is the greater of $10 or 1 percent.
  • Later, the penalty becomes the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent, with interest counted from January 1.
  • After five years of delinquency a property can go to tax sale.

Selling with taxes owed is workable, because the title company can pay the balance from your proceeds. Also ask how this year's tax will be divided between you and the buyer.

Recording fees

Recording a deed with the Weber County Recorder costs $45.00 for page one under HB 38 and nothing for further standard pages. A page bigger than 8.5 by 14 inches adds $2.00, and so does each description beyond 10.

Your options for selling a Roy house

Roy owners typically weigh three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell for cash. The timeline and up-front cost differ for each.

  • Listing reaches more buyers, though it brings showings, post-inspection repair requests and the chance a loan falls through.
  • Selling it yourself saves the commission and hands marketing, contracts and disclosures to you.
  • A cash sale can close on your date with the house taken as is, a fit for inherited, tenant-occupied or neglected homes.

After decades of ownership, a Roy house may carry deferred maintenance. Request a cash offer and set it beside what you would net after repairs, carrying costs and a longer wait. Nothing obliges you to accept.

Frequently asked questions

Is Roy, Utah in Weber County?

Yes, and Weber County mails the property tax bills.

When are Roy property taxes due?

November 30, unless it lands on a weekend or holiday. After that the bill is delinquent from December 1, carrying a penalty of the greater of $10 or 1 percent if cleared by January 31.

What is the deadline to appeal a property valuation in Roy?

Whichever is later of September 15 and 45 days after the valuation notice. Appeals go to the Weber County Board of Equalization, and late ones are limited to severe circumstances.

Does a Roy house need repairs before a cash sale?

No. A cash buyer can purchase a Roy house in its current condition. It still helps to tell the buyer about known problems such as roof leaks, an old furnace or unpermitted work.

Can I sell an inherited house in Roy?

Yes, once you have the legal authority to sell, for example as the personal representative or as an owner on the title. Talk with a Utah attorney or title company about the paperwork, then ask for a cash offer if you want a quick closing.

Battle Creek was the original name, taken from an 1849 clash between settlers and a small band of Ute people. A nearby cottonwood grove inspired the later name. Settlement began in 1850 and incorporation came on January 18, 1855. Once you say yes, the title or escrow company opens the file and orders a title search. Timpanogos, a new district, replaces Alpine School District on July 1, 2027, and Pleasant Grove is assigned to it. Verify with the boundary map.

File with the Utah County Board of Equalization by September 15, online, by email, by mail or in person.

Second homes explain part of the vacancy. The county water district says they exceed 20% of homes in Washington County.

Desert heat and what buyers inspect

This is a hot, dry desert city, so roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes wear fastest. St. George, in the same valley, averages a 101.9 degree July high and a 28.4 degree January low, and its record of 118 degrees came on July 4, 2007.

Expect a buyer's walk-through to focus on:

  • How old the air conditioner is and how well it works, since it runs for months.
  • Whether roof underlayment and tile or shingles have held up to years of sun.
  • Stucco cracks, faded paint and sun damage on south-facing walls and decks.
  • Irrigation lines and pool equipment, which break more often in extreme heat.

Put-off repairs here are a common reason listings linger, and a common reason owners consider an as-is sale where the buyer accepts the house in its current condition.

Water rules and yards

Water limits what a yard here can look like. Washington County's towns draw on the Virgin River basin and already use over 90% of its dependable yearly supply, so the rules keep tightening.

Most cities now limit turf on new residential lots to 8% of the lot area, with a separate limit on large lots. Turf is not allowed in park strips, in strips under 8 feet wide, or on slopes. Where secondary or reuse water exists, developers must use it for irrigation. Watering with drinking water is off limits between 10 a.m. and 8 p.m. in summer, and heavy users above a monthly volume pay an excessive water use fee of $1.00 per 1,000 gallons.

Before you rip out or replant a yard, look at the city's water conservation form. On an older lot, a big lawn means a bigger water bill, and buyers notice.

Shopping, schools and new competition

The city has three Interstate 15 exits. Exit 13 is billed as the gateway to the county and anchors the Green Springs master-planned community, a hospital and an auto mall. Near Exit 10 you will find a Walmart Supercenter, The Home Depot, Kohl's, Best Buy, Albertsons and In-N-Out, per a 2022 retail profile prepared for the city.

That profile also counts more than 3,300 homes added from 2017 through 2021, some of them denser multifamily buildings near Exit 13. Washington belongs to the Washington County School District, and families will want to know which school your address feeds. Get the boundary confirmed before you advertise.

Permits and city rules before you sell

Anything you build or finish before listing should be permitted. In Washington City the Building Department covers single-family permits, additions, basement finishes, demolition, detached accessory buildings, garages and shops, sheds and patio covers, pools and solar.

  • An accessory dwelling unit may require a deed restriction.
  • Visit the department at 111 North 100 East or call (435) 656-6326.

A buyer's inspector often spots unpermitted work such as a finished basement. If you are unsure what a past owner did, ask the department before you list.

Property tax and recording when you sell

Washington County collects real property tax once a year, with payment due November 30. The bill attaches to the parcel rather than to you, so an unpaid balance travels with the house to the next owner. The Treasurer mails each owner a notice, and the title company splits the year's bill between you and the buyer at closing. The Treasurer takes partial payments of $10 or more per parcel at any time, but there are no payment plans for delinquent balances. After five years or more of delinquency, a parcel can be offered at the county tax sale each May.

Utah applies a 45% residential exemption, so a home you live in is assessed on 55% of market value. A second home or a vacant house gets no exemption and is assessed at full value. If you moved out and kept the house, look at your bill before you list.

The Washington County Recorder, at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George, records the deed. Expect $45.00 per document and $2.00 for each legal description past the tenth. The office stops accepting recordings at 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time.

Three routes are open to you: hire an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer from an investor. Each swaps speed, price and effort differently. An agent listing reaches the most buyers, though you will live through showings, inspection requests and a closing date tied to the buyer's mortgage approval.

Cash fits when the house needs work, when a move is coming, or when you inherited property here and would rather not manage it. Cash Home Buyers makes offers on houses in any condition, and asking for one does not commit you. There are no showings, no appraisal delays and little repair haggling, and you pick the closing date that suits you.

Problems Washington sellers run into

A handful of issues come up again and again with Washington sellers.

  • Sun-baked roofs, stucco and air conditioners that buyers will discount.
  • Out-of-state heirs who now own a Washington County house.
  • Second-home owners surprised by full-value taxation.
  • New construction near Exit 13 and the Washington Fields area pulling buyers away from resale houses.
  • Unpermitted or half-finished projects that turn up in an inspection.

Whichever applies, begin by pulling together the deed, your latest tax notice and any permit records. Buyers, title companies and cash buyers all ask for those first.

No. Washington is a city, and Washington County is the county that contains it along with St. George, Hurricane and other communities. Property tax bills and deeds in the city go through county offices in St. George.

When are property taxes due in Washington, Utah?

Real property taxes are due November 30 each year. The County Treasurer mails the notice, and if you never receive one you are still responsible for the bill. The Treasurer's Office can send a copy on request.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Washington County?

The fee is $45.00 per document, plus $2.00 for each legal description over ten. Recordings are not accepted after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time.

Do I need a permit for work on my Washington house?

Usually yes for additions, basement finishes, pools, solar and detached buildings. Washington City's Building Department issues permits through its City Inspect portal. Call (435) 656-6326 if you are not sure.

Midvale at a glance

Midvale is a small, tightly built city, with the Jordan River on one side and Interstate 15 through its middle. The 2020 count was 36,028 people, against 27,964 in 2010, and much of that growth was new housing on former smelter land to the west.

Just 43.4% of Midvale homes are lived in by their owners. So the person selling is often a landlord, an heir to a rental, or an owner with a tenant still inside. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $436,600. Median gross rent is $1,597, households average 2.30 people, and density is 6,092 people per square mile. All of this describes the city broadly and says little about one particular house.

Bingham Junction and the old slag site

Bingham Junction is 446 acres on the west side where five smelters worked lead and copper ore from 1871 to 1958. The EPA lists the ground as the Midvale Slag Superfund site. A Ready for Reuse Determination in 2008 cleared it for commercial and residential use.

It now holds a light rail station that opened in 2011, a mix of housing types, offices, a supermarket and a park. Just south, Jordan Bluffs covers 351 acres of the same slag ground. Building there is still early, though proposals could bring around 3,500 homes.

Own a house on the west side? Lenders and buyers sometimes ask about the area's past. Dig out whatever closing or cleanup papers you got at purchase, and ask the title company about the specific parcel. Expect buyers near the station to weigh your house against newer townhomes and condos.

Rail, highways and main streets

Two TRAX lines, Interstate 15 and a quick hop to Interstate 215 keep most valley commutes manageable. Average travel time to work is 20.6 minutes.

  • The Red Line serves Bingham Junction and continues to the University of Utah.
  • The Blue Line serves Midvale Fort Union and Midvale Center.
  • 7800 South is the main east-west street, and Main Street (700 West) runs through the historic downtown.
  • The I-15 and I-215 interchange is near 7200 South and State Street, where a ski bus also runs.

Shopping clusters at the Shops at Fort Union and along State Street. A house within walking distance of a station should say so in its listing.

Older homes and earthquake risk

Midvale's west side grew around rail and smelting, and the east side moved from farmland to housing. Nearly all of the housing is under a century old, with many homes built in recent decades.

The bigger concern is the ground. The Wasatch Fault runs along the valley, and experts put the odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake somewhere on it within 50 years at 57 percent. Soft Lake Bonneville sediments under much of the Wasatch Front raise liquefaction risk. A magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna in March 2020 was felt across the valley.

An inspector going through an older Midvale house will likely flag chimneys, water heater strapping and foundation cracks. You can fix them, disclose them, or sell as-is and let the buyer decide.

Landlord business license

Renting out a house in Midvale takes a landlord business license from city hall. Yours runs out on August 31 and the renewal deadline is September 15. Most other business licenses run out December 31 and are late after January 15.

The council sets fees each year, and a business that relocates within Midvale gets new inspections. If you rent the house you are selling, make sure the license is paid up before an agent asks. The business licensing office can answer questions about your account.
