Whoever buys and moves in must apply, with filings due at the county Board of Equalization by September 15. Tell a buyer about it, since skipping the form means taxes on the full value.

Recording a deed with the county

Take a deed to the county recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600. The counter is staffed Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The office will not write a document for you, notarize it, or judge whether the title is clean.

Once a deed is processed and imaged, the original comes back by mail in two to three weeks. A title company normally files on your behalf, so a visit is rarely needed.

How a cash sale works in Midvale

Midvale deeds get recorded the usual way, yet a cash deal drops the lender, the appraiser and the back-and-forth over repairs. Here is the sequence.

  1. Tell us what the place is like: who lives there, what needs work, what paperwork is missing.
  2. We look it over and send a price.
  3. Say yes, and a title company sets up the signing and files the deed.
  4. Pick a closing day that suits you and the title company.

A rental with tenants, a house with deferred maintenance or one with inherited paperwork can go as-is. Saying no to our price costs you nothing. Ahead of that first conversation, collect the lease and rent roll, the newest tax notice and anything on the property's history.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with tenants in place

A tenant in the house does not stop you from selling. Put the lease and rent roll in the buyer's hands early, so the closing day can work around when the lease ends. Landlords should confirm that the city license is up to date and the tax bill is paid. A balance left after December 1 is delinquent and is cleared out of the proceeds at closing.

Paperwork to gather before you sell

A little preparation keeps a Midvale sale moving. Look for your deed or closing statement, the latest valuation and tax notices, any landlord license renewal, tenant leases with the rent roll, and receipts for major repairs. If the house came to you through an estate, add whatever probate or transfer papers exist. Yes, and many here do. Share the lease and rent roll with the buyer at the outset so the closing date matches the lease.

Springville at a glance

Springville nestles against the Wasatch Range in Utah County, nearly all of it east of Interstate 15 and roughly 3 miles from Utah Lake's average shoreline. Locals call it Art City, after the Springville Museum of Art, which dates to about 1937. Many residents drive to work in Provo-Orem or Salt Lake City, so freeway access weighs on buyers' minds. Houses near an I-15 exit are easiest to reach, and a seller can point to that.

Between 2010 and 2020 the population rose 19.7%. Owners occupy about seven in ten homes. Read the median as a survey result and not as an estimate for your own address.

Rental units, ADUs and short-term stays

Renting out part of your house is possible, though the city attaches ownership and occupancy conditions. ADUs belong only in single-family residential zones, so duplexes, twin homes and apartments are out.

  • The owner needs a stake of 50% or more in the property.
  • One of the two units has to be owner-occupied, so the main house and the ADU cannot both be rentals.
  • Interior conversions and detached ADUs both need a building permit.
  • A stay shorter than 30 days counts as short-term and calls for a city business license, with the host living in the main dwelling and on hand.

Leasing the upstairs and downstairs to different tenants turns on the zone, and on whether the second unit was legally permitted or counts as a legal nonconforming use. Never permitted your basement apartment? Say so to the buyer before anyone signs.

Building permits and inspections

A permit is needed ahead of any work that enlarges, repairs, alters, adds to or tears down a structure, or that installs equipment in it. Ask the city's building division which jobs state guidelines exempt.

Expect an inspection within three business days of asking, never the same day. Anything submitted after 5:00 p.m. on Friday, through Sunday night, is treated as received Monday. Call the building office at 801-489-2704. If a project is still open or was never finished, close it out with the city before you sell, because an open permit can slow a closing and make a buyer nervous.

A remodel done without a permit may prompt questions from a buyer's inspector or lender. Request your permit history from the city before listing.

Utilities and trash

Power, water and public works are all city departments. The Springville Power Department operates the Whitehead Power Plant and has a Customer Generation program that covers solar systems. Call (801) 489-2750 for outages and billing questions.

The culinary water system publishes a yearly water quality report, and recycling is picked up every other week. A buyer moving in will need to set up city utility accounts, so put that on your closing checklist.

Earthquakes and radon

Inspections sometimes turn up both. Ten segments make up the Wasatch Fault, and five are active, the Provo segment among them. Forecasters give a 57% chance of a quake of magnitude 6.0 or greater within 50 years.

Elevated radon turns up in one of every three Utah homes, and the action level is 4 picocuries per liter. Run a short test before you list so the result holds no surprise. If the reading is high, you can fix it or sell as is and let the price reflect it.

Due dates and penalties

Springville property is billed by Utah County, and a payment after November 30 draws a penalty. The county Auditor sends a valuation notice every year, and the tax notice itself follows in the second half of October. A home you live in is 45% exempt.

Visit the Treasurer at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1200 in Provo, or phone 801-851-8255. Earlier delinquencies are absent from the bill, so request a payoff figure. Your deed is filed by the Recorder, Suite 1300, 801-851-8179.

Think the value is wrong? The Board of Equalization takes filings until September 15, or 45 days after the notice goes out if that is later. After that the listed value is final for the year. Attach nearby sales and repair estimates.

How a cash sale works in Springville

Paying cash means no mortgage, no appraisal and no waiting on a loan decision. Describe the house, read the written offer and choose when to close.

Settlement happens at a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded in Provo. Taxes are split by days of ownership. Mention any unpermitted ADU or addition at the outset. Back taxes are listed by the title company and paid out of what you receive.

Before requesting offers, round up permit records, ADU paperwork, a recent utility bill and your mortgage payoff amount. With an inherited house, either empty it first or tell the buyer what remains and ask if they will accept it that way.

Selling a house with an unpermitted unit

Work done without a permit, such as an apartment or an addition, will not make a house unsellable, but it shapes the talks. Raise it with the buyer early. A mortgage lender may refuse to count a unit missing from the records, and that can sink a financed purchase near the end.

Two routes exist. One is to seek the permit and fix the work before listing, which costs time and money. The other is a cash buyer who accepts the house in its current state and sorts out the legal side later. With a tenant in place, share the lease and rent history, and keep the owner-occupancy rules above in mind when describing what a new owner may do.

From first call to closing

  1. Give us the address, the condition and your timing.
  2. Read the written offer and ask questions.
  3. Accept it, sign the purchase agreement and a title company opens the file.
  4. Title staff confirm ownership and taxes and draft the closing statement.
  5. You sign, the deed is recorded in Provo and payment follows.

With no loan involved there is no appraisal to wait for, so speed depends on title work and your own calendar.

Problems sellers run into

  • A basement apartment lacking a permit or a clear record of owner occupancy.
  • Nightly rentals where the host did not live in the main dwelling.
  • Remodeling finished without a building permit.
  • Possessions left inside an inherited house.

Disclose any that apply. A buyer who hears it from you early rarely walks away later.

Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. Notices go out in the second half of October.

Can I have a basement apartment in Springville?

Only as a permitted ADU in a single-family zone, with the owner holding at least 50% and living in one of the two units. A building permit is needed.

How many people live in Springville?

About 35,268 people in 2020, a 19.7% rise over the 29,466 counted in 2010.

Does a Springville short-term rental need a license?

Yes. Stays under 30 days require a city business license, and the host must live in the main dwelling and be present.

Kearns housing in brief

It packs 36,723 people from the 2020 count into 4.63 square miles, about 7,932 per square mile, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 35,404. Lots are small and neighbors are close, so a vacant or neglected house is easy to spot from the street.

From Army air base to suburb

Kearns began on May 1, 1942, as Kearns Army Air Base, a World War II training site named for Utah Senator Thomas Kearns. It became Camp Kearns on January 1, 1944 and was deactivated on August 15, 1946, when ownership moved to the State of Utah. Developers built homes and shops on the old base land, and the neighborhoods followed its street layout and foundations.

  • A base chapel became part of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church.
  • A base train station later served as a day-care center.
  • A base theater became part of Kearns Junior High School.

The population reached 17,172 in 1960 and 21,353 by 1980, with later building extending west of the railroad tracks to 5600 West. A house from those decades invites questions about original roofing, wiring and plumbing.

Cityhood and who provides services

Cityhood came on May 1, 2024, through Utah House Bill 35. Earlier the area was an unincorporated community, a township from June 1, 2002, and then a metro township effective January 1, 2017. In the 1990s residents gathered enough signatures to keep West Valley City and West Jordan from annexing them.

Everyday services still run through shared providers. Unified Police and Unified Fire cover public safety. Permits, business licenses, zoning, code enforcement and stormwater all go through the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District, at 860 W. Levoy Dr., Suite 300, Taylorsville, phone 385-910-5600. The mayor's office is at 4250 W 5415 S, by appointment, at 385-855-8375.

As a city, Kearns gained new tax options, including a property tax and a telecommunications tax, and planned a redevelopment agency. Watch the city's budget and agenda pages if future taxes matter to you.

The Utah Olympic Oval, at 5662 South Cougar Lane, was built in 2001 for the 2002 Winter Olympics. The five-acre facility has Utah's only 400-meter speed skating oval, two international-size ice sheets and a four-lane, 442-meter running track. The Oquirrh Recreation and Parks District runs public skating, Learn to Skate classes and curling, and rents skates. Kearns High School and the schools of the Granite School District serve the city, and a new Kearns Library opened in December 2020. For a listing, these are easy local selling points.

Winter weather and earthquakes

Winters are cold and summers warm and mostly dry. In a normal year the county sees about 15 inches of precipitation and 55 inches of snow, and winter inversions can hold smog in the valley. Expect early questions about how old the roof and furnace are.

Utah's most active fault runs along the Wasatch. Liquefaction risk is highest in the low middle of a valley with shallow groundwater, especially close to lakes and streams. Susceptible soils are loose, young, sandy or silty deposits saturated within about 30 to 50 feet of the surface. Kearns sits on the old Lake Bonneville bed, so checking the geological maps for your lot is sensible.

  • The maps show general patterns only.
  • One lot needs a site study by a qualified Utah engineer and geologist.
  • The most recent large quake on the Salt Lake City segment struck about 1,400 years back.

Appeals to the Board of Equalization cover this year's market value alone, and the bill stays payable while the case is pending. A recent purchase, a fee appraisal, or three to five comparable sales all count as proof. Call the Treasurer at 385-468-8300 about relief programs.

Only 55% of your main home's value is taxed, since 45% is exempt. To qualify you must live there for at least 183 consecutive days in a year. Whoever buys the house files a new claim of their own.

A title or escrow company closes the deal, and the Salt Lake County Recorder at 2001 South State Street files the deed. Under the October 2024 schedule the flat fee was $40, and the paper needs a Salt Lake County legal description, the parcel number and an original notarized signature.

  • The grantee's mailing address must appear on the deed.
  • Use white paper, 8.5 by 11 inches, with clear space at the top of the first page.
  • Originals come back by mail two to three weeks after processing.
  • The Recorder does not draft or notarize documents. The phone is 385-468-8145.

The title company normally manages these details, but check that every name on the deed matches the signature page.

Any unpaid property tax is paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for the balance, give it to the title officer, and the year's bill is split between you and the buyer.

You send us the street address and a few details about the house. We look it over and compare recent sales close by, then give you a number you can accept or decline. If you accept, the title company runs a search, schedules the signing and records the deed at the county, and your money arrives at closing. Houses on tight Kearns lots rarely need a long explanation, so the process tends to move quickly once the paperwork is in order.

Without a lender there is no loan approval to wait on and no bank repair demands. You avoid staging, photos and open houses. The title company still verifies who owns the home and clears any liens before closing, and you help choose the closing date.

Sellers can list, sell privately or take a cash offer. Listing means preparing the house, paying commission and waiting on a buyer's loan. A cash sale lets the house go in its present state.

The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District handles building permits, business licensing, land use, zoning, code enforcement and stormwater. Its main number is 385-910-5600.

Those houses are now about fifty years old, so a seller may be weighing repairs to the roof, furnace or plumbing before listing.

From copper mill town to city

Magna began as a farming and ranching settlement, and pioneers started arriving in 1851. The turning point came in 1906, when the Utah Copper Company began building the Magna Mill. The name comes from the Latin word for great and was officially adopted on October 19, 1915. Older neighborhoods around Main Street went by names such as Greektown, Japantown, Snaketown and Little Italy.

Magna became a township in 2001 and a metro township in 2017. It became a city on May 1, 2024, under Utah House Bill 35.

The March 2020 earthquake

A magnitude 5.7 earthquake hit at 7:09 a.m. on March 18, 2020, with its epicenter about 6 kilometers north-northeast of Magna. It was the strongest in Utah since the 1992 St. George quake. Nobody died and injuries were minor, but bricks fell from some buildings and about 145 historic structures were damaged. Cyprus High School took some of the worst damage. Building-related damage was put at about $62 million of $629 million in total losses.

If your house had quake repairs, keep the paperwork, since buyers ask what was fixed. A house with repairs still undone is one reason owners choose to sell as-is.

Northrop Grumman now runs a solid rocket motor plant in Magna.

Kennecott Land's West Bench plan calls for major development, including an urban center along I-80. Main Street has seen commercial decline and some vacant storefronts, though it was remodeled in 2006 and is a popular filming location. Compare recent nearby sales and do not assume the West Bench plan will lift your price. West 3500 South (SR-171) is the main east and west road, and South 8400 West (SR-111) is the main north and south road. UTA route 35 runs along 3500 South every 15 minutes on weekdays and loops through Main Street, and the TRAX Green Line is nearby.

The Granite School District serves Magna. Elementary schools are Copper Hills, Elk Run, Lake Ridge, Magna and Pleasant Green. Matheson Junior High is the middle school, and Cyprus High School competes at the 5A level.

Cut weeds, clear stored junk, move vehicles onto a hard surface and make sure any carport sits clear of the property line. These small fixes keep a violation notice from landing in the middle of a sale.

Then look inside. If the house is from the 1970s, note the age of the roof, furnace and water heater. Gather receipts for any quake repairs and permits for finished basements or additions. Buyers and inspectors ask about all of these, and clear answers keep a deal from stalling.

Clearfield's layout

Clearfield is a compact city in north-central Davis County, about 30 miles north of Salt Lake City, with Hill Air Force Base along its northeastern edge. It covers roughly 7.75 square miles. Sunset lies north, Clinton northwest, Syracuse and West Point west, and Layton wraps the south and east.

The streets run on a grid across flat ground, from about 4,314 feet at 1000 West and Antelope Drive to 4,711 feet in the northeast corner on base property. The Weber and Davis Canal runs along the east and northeast edge, and Interstate 15 follows the eastern side of town. Because the city is small, many houses are a short drive from the base gates, the Freeport Center and the freeway, and buyers ask about that first.

Hill Air Force Base and the local market

The base borders Clearfield, Layton, Riverdale, Roy and Sunset, with its longest border shared with Clearfield and Layton. It is Davis County's largest employer, with nearly 23,000 military and civilian personnel, and it accounts for about 12 percent of the county's economy. The 75th Air Base Wing hosts the Ogden Air Logistics Complex, the 388th and 419th Fighter Wings and more than 50 other units.

For a seller, that means a steady pool of local buyers and renters. It also means the occasional sudden move when someone gets orders and has little time to prepare a house. The Freeport Center, a 680-acre complex of 78 buildings with about 70 companies and roughly 7,000 workers, adds more local jobs. Two newer business areas, Legend Hills off I-15 and the planned Falcon Hill aerospace area, point to more aerospace work nearby.

Older houses and what buyers check

Much of the city's growth came after World War II. Population went from 982 in 1940 to 4,723 in 1950 and was 31,909 in 2020, so a good share of the houses are several decades old. Expect a mid-century house to draw questions about original kitchens, baths, electrical panels and plumbing.

The area gets about 20.75 inches of precipitation and about 24 inches of snow a year. Winter inversions can trap heavy air pollution along this part of the Wasatch Front, so buyers may care about filters and furnace condition. The Wasatch Fault runs along the western base of the mountains, and the Utah Division of Emergency Management warns that older unreinforced masonry buildings face greater risk in a strong quake.

  • Furnace, filters and ductwork on 1950s and 1960s homes
  • Brick chimneys and masonry porches
  • Roof age after years of snow load
  • Drainage and grading on lots near the Weber and Davis Canal

Commuting by rail and road

A FrontRunner commuter rail stop opened in Clearfield in 2008, and Davis County counts the city among its station cities, alongside Woods Cross, Farmington and Layton. Interstate 15 is the other main route. Clearfield High School, North Davis Junior High and elementary schools such as South Clearfield, Hill Field and Holt are in the Davis School District.

How Davis County bills Clearfield property tax

Davis County sends the bill, and payment is due November 30. When that date falls on a weekend, the treasurer moves it to the next business day, December 1 or December 2 depending on the calendar.

Ways to pay a Davis County property tax bill

Card payments carry a fee that goes to the card company. Electronic checks do not. After November 30 the penalty is the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent per parcel, falling to the greater of $10 or 1 percent if you pay in full by January 31. Interest of 7.25 to 10 percent follows after that.

Residential reduction and rentals

Utah Code 59-2-103 gives residential property a 45 percent reduction in value, so a primary residence is taxed on 55 percent. Rental houses do not get it unless the tenant lives there as a primary residence, so Clearfield landlords often see a higher bill.

The title company divides the year's tax bill between you and the buyer by the closing date. Ask for that proration in writing. If your lender has been paying the tax from escrow, confirm that, since the county notes that third-party services can be slow to post payments.

  1. Pull your latest Davis County tax notice.
  2. Confirm whether a lender escrow account pays it.
  3. Give the notice and payoff details to the title company.
  4. Check the proration line on the closing statement.

Selling on a short timeline

When orders or a job change force a fast move, the order of work matters more than the speed of any one step. Start with the paper that takes the longest to get: the payoff letter from your lender, the lease if a tenant is in place, and the tax notice from Davis County. Those three tell the title company what must be cleared before it can set a closing date.

Next, decide what you will do about repairs. A house with an original furnace, an older panel or a worn roof does not have to be fixed for a cash buyer to take it, but you should say what is wrong. Clear notes on the roof, heating, plumbing and electrical prevent surprises that could push the date back.

If a lender escrow account has been paying your tax, ask the servicer for the payment history before you list. A missed posting is easy to fix now and much harder to fix at the closing table.

Finally, plan the move-out. Utilities, mail and keys all need dates, and a fixed closing day makes each of them easier to arrange.

What does a quick sale look like for a Clearfield seller?

Clearfield sellers often own a mid-century house with deferred updates, a rental that has run its course, or a home they must sell quickly because of a job or military move. A cash sale closes on a date you choose and skips the repair requests that come with a lender's appraisal. The path is simple: you describe the house, take or decline an offer, and a title company handles the search and paperwork.

  • Houses with original kitchens, baths, electrical panels and plumbing
  • Rentals where tenants have moved out and left repairs
  • Homes owned by someone who has relocated for work
  • Inherited property with several heirs and no clear plan

Base assignments can change fast, and orders rarely arrive on a seller's timeline. If you are in that spot, tell the buyer your move date at the start so it can be built into the closing schedule.

Davis County. The treasurer's office in Farmington bills the property tax, and its phone number is 801-451-3243.

What is the property tax due date in Clearfield?

November 30. If that is a weekend, the due date moves to the next business day, and penalties start after that day.

What is the Freeport Center in Clearfield?

A 680-acre manufacturing and distribution complex on the former Clearfield Naval Supply Depot, with 78 buildings, about 70 companies and roughly 7,000 workers.

Does Hill Air Force Base affect Clearfield housing?

Yes. The base is next door and is Davis County's largest employer, with nearly 23,000 personnel, so many local homes are bought and sold by people tied to it.

Can I sell a Clearfield house that needs repairs?

Yes. Houses can sell as they are, with repairs left undone. Tell the buyer about the roof, heating, plumbing and electrical so terms are clear before closing.

The 2020 count found 32,945 people in 8,958 households, and only 2.4% of the 9,175 housing units stood vacant. On a street where almost every house is occupied, a neglected or empty one stands out fast.

How Kaysville got its name

Hector Haight came north in 1847 looking for feed for livestock. The settlement later honored William Kay, who became bishop of the local ward in 1851. It was first called Kay's Ward. Residents once asked to rename it Freedom, and Brigham Young answered, 'When did Kay's Ward get its Freedom.' The name stuck. Kaysville was incorporated on March 15, 1868, the first city in Davis County. The history is a talking point, but buyers today care far more about the roof, the permits and the price.

Work, commuting and moving timelines

Davis County is a bedroom community, and many residents drive to Salt Lake County. Hill Air Force Base, up in the northern part of the county, employs nearly 23,000 military and civilian workers and is the biggest single employer. Other big employers include the Davis School District, Lagoon Amusement Park and Lifetime Products.

Kaysville City Power is at 721 W Old Mill Lane, phone 801-544-8925.

Building permit fees and expired permits

Kaysville prices permits by project value, then adds a 1% state education fee and a 25% plan check fee. The city posts a fee schedule online, along with impact fees for building a new house.

Work that never starts within 180 days, or sits idle for 180 days, kills the permit and costs you the construction bond. Say your half-finished basement carries a dead permit. Renting part of your Kaysville house

The city permits internal accessory dwelling units under Kaysville City Code 17-31-3, with one condition: the owner has to occupy either the main house or the unit as a primary residence.

Valuation notices leave the Davis County offices at the end of July. The appeal cutoff under Utah law is whichever comes later, September 15 or 45 days after the auditor's notice, so phone Tax Administration for the exact date before filing.

Only market value is appealable, never the rate. County commissioners sit as the Board of Equalization and rely on hearing officers they appoint. Bring closing documents, a certified appraisal or comparable sales. An agent who files for you needs notarized authorization.

  • The Tax Administration office is in Farmington at 61 South Main Street, Room 101.
  • Phone: 801-451-3331 or 801-451-3329.
  • Late appeals can be heard by the board when circumstances are extenuating.

Under the primary residential exemption, a qualifying home is taxed on just 55% of market value. That status does not carry over, so warn the buyer that a new application is due after closing.

A bill still open at closing comes out of your proceeds, with the year divided between you and the buyer. Request the proration number early so your net payout holds no surprises.

How a cash sale closes in Kaysville

Closing happens at a title company, and the Davis County Recorder files the deed. Without a loan the sequence is short: purchase contract, title search, signed settlement statement, recording.

Utah requires the deed to name the grantees, show a mailing address for assessment and tax purposes, and carry a legal description that meets state standards. Expect the recorder to ask for the parcel's tax identification number as well.

There is no mortgage underwriting, so nothing hangs on a lender's appraisal, and no bank-driven repair list stands between you and the closing table. You do not stage rooms, host open houses or schedule strangers through the home. The offer is based on the house as it is today, and you pick the closing window that fits your move, whether that is quick or a few weeks out.

The steps stay simple and few. You share the address, we review the property and nearby sales, you accept or decline, and the title company handles the search, the signing and the filing at the county.

This is a young, family-oriented city, with a median age of 29.9 and 52.4% of households raising children under 18. An empty house after a move or a death looks out of place, and the carrying costs keep running.

Whatever you choose, work out the net after repairs, commission and holding costs, and read every contract before signing.

Gather the deed, the newest tax notice, permits for any finished basement or remodel, and paperwork on a basement apartment. Yes, as an internal accessory dwelling unit, provided you live in the house or the unit. Add a paved parking space of its own, and get a permit if the tenant is not family.

Who provides sewer service in Kaysville?

Central Davis Sewer provides sewer service, not the city. The city provides water, power, pressure irrigation, garbage, recycling and storm water.

Do building permits expire in Kaysville?

Yes. Work that does not begin within 180 days, or halts for 180 days, ends the permit. You lose the bond and must apply again.

Short-term rentals need a city license and are allowed mainly in multi-family residential areas, within condominium or homeowners association communities. If your unit has been used that way, confirm the license status before you sell.

Estates take the most coordination. Every heir who must sign needs to be identified early, and the title company will want the paperwork that shows who has authority to sell. Starting that conversation before you ask for an offer shortens the timeline.

Permit history and older additions

Holladay was a county community until it incorporated in 1999, and a house remodeled before then can have a murky permit trail. Check with the building office on whether an older addition or basement finish was ever closed out. A plan described in October 2024 calls for 614 residential units and up to 750,000 square feet of shops, restaurants and offices, with a 147-unit apartment building and a 38-townhome project already underway. Some townhomes were listed at $1 million or more.

All that building shifts the yardstick for nearby sellers. A buyer touring a decades-old house may also be touring a new townhome, so the older house has to earn its price on lot, location or condition. If it needs work, an as-is sale sidesteps the comparison.

Schools and city offices

The Granite School District serves Holladay. Olympus High School, open since 1953, is the lone public high school inside city limits. Look up the assigned school for an address on the district site rather than guessing from the street.

The Community Development office handles planning and building and answers at 801-527-3890. Salt Lake County handles assessment, tax collection and recording.

Permit rules that can affect a sale

The city wants a building permit for additions, remodels of any size, basement finishes, reroofing, solar, pools, spas and front-yard fencing, and grants a Certificate of Occupancy once final inspections pass.

Plenty of work is exempt: decks under 18 inches above grade, backyard fences up to 6 feet, like-for-like swaps of plumbing fixtures, lights and receptacles, plus cabinets, trim, carpet and paint. A shed of 200 square feet or less and under 20 feet tall skips the building permit but still gets a zoning check.

  • Removing a tree on public or private property can need a permit under city code sections 13.77.080 and 13.77.090.
  • Fences in front yards stop at 4 feet, while side and rear yards can go to 6 feet.
  • After a Correction Notice you generally get about 30 days to cure the violation.
  • HOA covenants are enforced by each subdivision's association, not by city planners.

A basement or addition without a permit will not block a cash deal. It does stop many financed ones, because appraisers and lenders ask what is legal. Selling in current condition avoids that argument.

Earthquake and soil questions

Holladay is on the Wasatch Front, home to Utah's most active fault, and the Utah Geological Survey maps liquefaction across these valleys. The most recent big quake on the Salt Lake City segment was about 1,400 years back. Magnitude 7 events have repeated about every 1,300 years.

Low ground with shallow groundwater is where liquefaction is most likely, so exposure varies by lot. The maps show broad patterns only, and a particular lot needs a study by a qualified Utah engineer and geologist.

Older brick is the bigger worry. Unreinforced masonry from roughly the 1920s to the 1960s was not built for sideways shaking, so owners of brick houses from that era should expect questions about bracing and chimney anchors.

Property tax dates

Holladay tax bills come from Salt Lake County. The assessed value is fixed on January 1, payment for the year is due November 30, and anything unpaid goes delinquent December 1.

Tax stepWhenWhat happens
Value setJanuary 1Lien date for the year
Valuation noticesJuly and AugustShow the assessed value
Appeal windowJuly 31 to September 15Board of Equalization hears cases
Tax noticesBy November 1Treasurer collects
Last day without penaltyNovember 30Delinquent December 1

Only this year's market value can be argued, and you need backing such as a recent purchase price, an appraisal or three or more comparable sales. The Treasurer's office, at 385-468-8300, also takes applications for tax relief programs. Details are on the Salt Lake County tax administration page.

Primary residential exemption

Your main residence is taxed on 55% of its market value since 45% is exempt. That break stays with you and does not transfer. Whoever buys must file their own claim, and skipping it can mean tax on the full value for the year. A house that was rented out has its own declaration step.

How a cash sale closes in Holladay

Closing runs through a title or escrow company, and the deed is filed with the Salt Lake County Recorder. Since no lender is involved, nothing waits on an appraisal or a loan decision.

The October 2024 schedule sets a flat $40 per recording. Paperwork must include the Salt Lake County legal description, the parcel number, an original notarized signature and the buyer's mailing address. Staff there will not draft or notarize anything or hand out forms, and originals come back by mail roughly two to three weeks after imaging. Questions go to 385-468-8145.

  • Start the title search sooner if a family trust or an estate held the house.
  • Make sure every name on the deed is spelled the same on the signature page and the notary block.
  • Have the title officer split the year's tax bill between you and the buyer.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Your options as a Holladay seller

Three routes are open: hire an agent, sell on your own or accept a cash offer. A listing means cleanup, repairs and showings while new townhomes pull in the same shoppers. A cash buyer accepts the place in its present state.

  • Inherited houses where maintenance slipped, common in the older neighborhoods.
  • Rentals with tenants still living there, which makes showings awkward.
  • Houses with a basement or addition built without a permit.
  • Owners behind on payments who need a firm closing date.

Weigh any offer against the net from a listing after repairs, commission and holding costs, and get the closing date and proof of funds in writing.

Selling with taxes owed

If the year's bill is unpaid when you sell, the title company prorates it and pays it from your proceeds at closing. Call the Treasurer's office for the balance and pass it to the title officer ahead of time.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Holladay house with an unpermitted basement?

Yes. A cash buyer can purchase the house as it is, though the missing permit may lower the price. Financed buyers and their appraisers often object, so a regular listing may require closing out the work first through the Holladay building office.

When is property tax due on a Holladay home?

November 30 each year, billed by the Salt Lake County Treasurer. Taxes become delinquent on December 1. If you sell mid-year, the title company normally prorates the bill at closing.

Does the new owner keep my primary residential exemption?

No. The exemption does not pass to a buyer automatically. The new owner applies with the county, and a missed filing can mean tax on the full market value for that year.

How long does recording the deed take in Salt Lake County?

The title company usually files it right after closing. The county returns original documents by mail about two to three weeks after imaging.

Is Holladay in a liquefaction or fault zone?

It depends on the lot. The Utah Geological Survey publishes liquefaction and fault maps for the Wasatch Front, and a particular property needs a site-specific study by a qualified Utah professional.

Getting around: freeways, TRAX and the S Line

Buyers like the transit and the freeways. At the northwest corner is the Spaghetti Bowl, where I-15, I-80 and SR-201 come together, and both I-15 and I-80 have local interchanges.

  • TRAX light rail runs along roughly 200 West with three stations in the city, and the Blue, Red and Green lines meet at Central Pointe station.
  • The S Line streetcar opened in December 2013 and stops at Central Pointe, South Main, 300 East and 500 East.

Work out the walk from your address to the nearest stop. Buyers and tenants raise that distance almost immediately.

Code enforcement

South Salt Lake polices yards, parked vehicles and property upkeep, and a first contact is usually a courtesy notice. Over 90% of issues end through conversation and education, but cases that drag on can bring fines and civil prosecution.

  • Lawns and ground cover must stay under 6 inches, and owners must control noxious weeds.
  • Vehicles belong on paved surfaces, not grass, dirt or gravel.
  • An inoperable or unregistered vehicle left 30 consecutive days is a public nuisance.
  • Trash bins go out by 7:00 a.m. on collection day and come back in afterward.
  • Sidewalks must be cleared of snow within 24 hours, leaving a path at least 42 inches wide.

An inherited house that was neglected may carry an open violation. Cleaning it up first takes one more worry off a buyer's list. The number to call about a specific property is 801-464-6757.

Rental licenses and short-term rentals

A landlord must hold a city license, and the Building Department and Fire Marshal inspect on site before one is issued. Renting without an approved license is a Class C misdemeanor.

Joining the Good Landlord Program means training every three years, written leases and background checks on adult occupants, and in return license fees drop significantly. A license cannot be transferred, so whoever buys a rental applies fresh.

For short-term stays, a pending ordinance issued October 15, 2026 stays in place for 180 days or until a new code is adopted. It defines a short-term rental as a stay under 30 consecutive days, requires an owner-occupied duplex, an owner-occupied rental or a property owned by a primary resident, and bars them in accessory dwelling units. Check the city's page for the final code before you plan on nightly rentals.

Due dates and penalties

The county mails the bill and expects payment by November 30. On December 1 any unpaid current-year real property tax is delinquent, and the penalty is the greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel. Pay in full by January 31 and it is cut to 1%.

A house you live in gets a 45% exemption, leaving 55% of market value taxable. Rentals and second homes get no such break, so an investment property's bill can look high.

The Treasurer is at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, and the Recorder, who files the deed, is in Suite N1-600 of the same building.

Appealing your valuation

Notices of valuation go in the mail by July 22. Your window to appeal to the Board of Equalization ends September 15, or 45 days after the notice if that is later. Back your case with recent sales of comparable homes and photos or estimates showing condition problems the valuation overlooks.

Bank underwriting never slows a cash buyer, a real plus for a house with put-off repairs or sitting tenants. Tell us the address, the condition and what you want from the sale, and a written offer follows.

The closing takes place at a title or escrow company, and the Salt Lake County Recorder records the deed. For a rental, settle lease, deposit and license questions with the buyer ahead of closing day, and provide every lease along with tenant payment records and any notices you sent. If the house is vacant, bring the keys, the utility account details and a list of anything left inside, so the handover is quick and nobody is surprised by what remains in the garage or basement.

Selling a rental house with tenants

Many sellers here own a rental, and a sale works best when the paperwork is ready. Tell the buyer up front whether the house is occupied, what each lease says and when it ends. Deposits belong to the tenants, so the title company needs to know where they are held and who takes responsibility for them after closing.

Because the city license does not move to a new owner, a buyer who plans to keep renting must pass the inspections and apply on their own. A buyer who plans to live in the house or renovate it has a different timeline. Knowing which kind of buyer you have shapes the closing date you can offer.

Ask the title company for a closing statement ahead of time. It lists the tax split, any payoff and the recording charge, so you can see what you will receive before you sign.

If the rental license has lapsed or an inspection was failed, fix what you can before showing the house, or tell the cash buyer so the offer reflects it.

Checks to run before you accept an offer

  • Does every unit in a duplex or converted basement have a building permit on file?
  • Is the rental license current, and were the inspections passed?
  • Is any code complaint open about weeds, vehicles or trash?
  • Who lives in the house, and must a lease or deposit transfer?

If a cash buyer hears these answers first, the offer comes out cleaner and late renegotiation becomes unlikely.

Which county is South Salt Lake in?

Salt Lake County. Its Assessor values your house, its Treasurer collects the tax and its Recorder files your deed.

When is South Salt Lake property tax due?

By November 30. After that the current-year tax is delinquent from December 1, with a lower 1% penalty for payment in full by January 31.

Do I need a license to rent out my South Salt Lake house?

Yes, and inspections by the Building Department and Fire Marshal come first. Renting without a license is a Class C misdemeanor, and Good Landlord certification cuts the fee.

Can I run a short-term rental in South Salt Lake?

Only under the pending ordinance issued October 15, 2026, which covers owner-occupied or primary-resident properties and bans ADUs. Check the city page for the final code.

How much is a house worth in South Salt Lake?

The median value of owner-occupied homes is $410,200 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, and your own house may sit above or below it.

The Farmington Trail Committee maintains 146.49 miles of trails, so a house near a trailhead has a selling point worth naming in any conversation.

Snow, floods and the irrigation system

Snowfall averages 48.6 inches a year, so shoppers study the roof and ask about leaks. Flash floods struck Farmington in the 1920s and 1930s and once more in 1984. If your lot sits close to a creek or a canyon mouth, ask an insurance agent whether flood coverage makes sense and be ready to tell a buyer what you learned.

Accessory dwelling unit rules

The city recognizes two accessory unit types and a third arrangement that carves a detached unit onto a lot of its own. Each single-family home may have one ADU, no more.

  • Internal ADU: built inside or attached to the main house, on a lot of at least 6,000 square feet.
  • Detached ADU: a permanent building on a foundation, on a lot of at least 10,000 square feet.
  • Subordinate single-family dwelling: its own home on its own lot, with subdivision approval.

Somebody must live on site, either in the main house or in the ADU. After a subordinate dwelling is split off, the owner has to occupy it for two years. Every unit needs a full kitchen, a full bathroom and a parking space off the street, in addition to the main home's parking. Tenants must stay 30 days or longer, which rules out nightly rentals.

Turning existing space into an internal ADU needs a building permit, unless that space was approved for living in the first place. An unpapered basement apartment can derail a buyer who needs a mortgage, so dig out whatever permits exist before showing the house.

Property taxes in Farmington

Davis County sends the bills, and Utah's statewide calendar governs the dates. Payment is due November 30. If the house is your main residence, the 45% exemption means only 55% of market value is taxed.

The Davis County Controller mails valuation notices at the close of July. Appeals must be filed by mid-September. Phone Tax Administration at 801-451-3331 to learn the exact cutoff. The office is in Room 101 at 61 South Main Street.

How to appeal your assessment

Appeals go to the Board of Equalization, which is the Davis County Commission. Only the market value is open to challenge, and the tax rate is not. Filing is limited to the owner or an agent with notarized authorization.

Evidence the board accepts:

  • a complete appraisal by a certified appraiser,
  • sales of at least three similar properties near January 1,
  • proof of a factual mistake, like an incorrect square footage.

If you cannot tell what you owe, call Tax Administration and ask for the balance on your parcel. Give that number to the title officer and closing day holds no surprises.

How a cash sale works in Farmington

Selling for cash here is simpler than a financed sale, since nobody at a bank has to approve the house. You tell us about it, we weigh it against neighboring sales, and the decision to accept stays with you.

  1. Send the address and a few basics.
  2. We study the house and recent sales around it.

Tell the title company early about an unpaid tax bill or an ADU that never got its permit, so each can be settled ahead of recording.

What a cash sale skips

Without a lender, a handful of familiar hurdles vanish: no loan approval to wait for, no appraisal that might come in short, and no repair list a bank insists on before funding. Photos, open houses and weeks of strangers touring the rooms also drop away.

Title work remains. The title company confirms ownership, searches for liens and drafts the closing papers. If a family trust or an estate holds the deed, say so at the outset, since that adds paperwork on the title side.

Common problems for Farmington sellers

Several situations show up before many sales here.

  • An older house in or near the Clark Lane Historic District that needs updating.
  • A basement apartment never permitted as an internal ADU.
  • A detached unit the owner would like to sell apart from the main house, which the city handles as a subordinate single-family dwelling.
  • A valuation notice the owner wants to dispute before selling.

Any of these can drag out a regular listing. A direct sale lets you skip staging and repairs and choose your own closing timeline. Mention them at the start and we will price the house with them in mind.

What to gather before you sell

Collect the deed, your latest tax notice, permits for additions or a basement unit, roof and repair records, and a note on how the yard is watered. With these in hand the title work moves faster and the first questions from a buyer already have answers.

What county is Farmington, Utah in?

Davis County. Farmington is the county seat, and the county's Tax Administration office is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101.

When are property taxes due in Farmington?

November 30, the statewide due date. Unpaid taxes become delinquent after that, with a reduced penalty if everything is paid by January 31.

How do I appeal my Farmington property value?

File with the Davis County Board of Equalization once the valuation notice arrives at the end of July. The deadline falls in mid-September, so confirm the date with Tax Administration. Only the market value can be appealed.

Can I rent out a Farmington ADU for short stays?

No. ADU rentals must run 30 days or longer, and the owner must live in either the main home or the ADU.

What size lot do I need for a detached ADU in Farmington?

At least 10,000 square feet. An internal ADU needs a lot of at least 6,000 square feet.

Hurricane housing in brief

Hurricane lies in southwestern Utah at the eastern end of the St. George area, and the Virgin River hugs nearly the whole northern boundary. Between 2010 and 2020 the population rose 45.7% to 20,036, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 25,745. Of 8,035 housing units counted in 2020, 13.1% stood vacant, so an empty house is a common sight and buyers have plenty of choices.

Local pulls for buyers

Hurricane began in 1896 as part of the Cotton Mission, and small farms around town still grow peaches, pecans and pistachios. Sand Hollow State Park has a 1,322-acre reservoir with camping and trails, and Quail Creek State Park offers a 600-acre reservoir and a campground. Distribution centers and an annual mountain bike festival bring work and visitors. A recreational trail follows the old Hurricane Canal, dry since 1985. Mentioning the lakes and trails helps a listing, but out-of-area shoppers still judge the house on heat, water and upkeep.

Desert heat and your roof

Summers are brutal. The nearest long-term weather record, from St. George, puts the typical July high near 101.9 degrees, with about 60 afternoons each year at 100 or hotter. Rainfall is only about 9 inches. Nights drop to 32 degrees or lower on roughly 60 mornings a year, and monsoon storms arrive from mid-July to mid-September.

Shoppers will ask about the age of the roof and the cooling system, so find those dates before the first showing. Look over the drainage around the lot too, since monsoon downpours show weak spots fast.

Water has made headlines here before. The Quail Creek dike, part of an offstream reservoir run by the Washington County Water Conservancy District, gave way at 12:30 a.m. on January 1, 1989 and released about 25,000 acre-feet. Damage ran to about $12 million, with no deaths.

City offices, schools and power

You can reach city offices at 147 N 870 W or by calling 435-635-2811. Business licensing is handled inside Planning and Zoning, and a home-based business can be approved under Title 10, Chapter 42 of city code.

Students attend Washington County schools, and Hurricane High School runs grades 10 to 12. Hurricane operates its own electric utility, which reports delivering power 99.9846% of the time. Fire response comes from the Hurricane Valley Fire District.

Short-term rentals and your sale

Section 3-10-11 of city code requires a business license for any short-term rental. Single-family zones have a cap, and no second rental license may sit within 300 feet of an existing one.

Rental ruleHurricane requirement
License cap, single-family zonesThree licenses per 1,000 residents

The license stays behind when you sell. Within 45 days of closing, the new owner must apply for a fresh one or the old one is forfeited, and then the buyer would need to reapply or wait in line. Say so at the start if the house has been a rental, because an investor may value that license as part of the price.

Due dates and tax sales

Washington County real property tax comes due every November 30, whether or not a notice reached you. Neighbors received one and you did not? Call the Treasurer for a copy. There are no payment plans, but any partial payment of $10 or more per parcel is accepted at any time.

  • Each payment covers interest first, then penalty, then tax. When several years are delinquent, Utah law sends the money to the newest year first.
  • The Clerk-Auditor holds a sale each May for properties delinquent five years or more.
  • Utah bans the sale of tax liens and tax lien certificates.

The tax is a lien on the land and not a debt of the person, and the title company divides the bill between buyer and seller on a mid-year sale. The Treasurer works from 111 East Tabernacle St. in St. George and answers at 435-301-7720.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Hurricane houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appeals and the exemption

Valuation appeals run on a state deadline: the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor sends notice. A main home is taxed on 55% of market value. Buyers must file their own claim for that exemption after they purchase.

Closing day paperwork

Closing takes place at a title company, and the deed then goes to the Washington County Recorder at 111 East Tabernacle in St. George. Recordings are not taken after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, so a late signing may be filed the next day. The Recorder's phone is 435-301-7680.

A deed must name the grantees, give a mailing address for tax billing and include a proper legal description. The signature must match the name of the owner of record, which is worth confirming at the start for an inherited house.

Selling with taxes owed

When a bill is still open at closing, it is paid from your proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff amount and hand it to the title officer. Since the lien follows the land, clearing it is built into every closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a cash sale works in Hurricane

Start by giving us the address and basic details. We tour the house, check what sold nearby, and make an offer you are free to decline. After you accept, a title company searches the record, chooses a closing date and files the deed. With no lender in the picture, you avoid an appraisal wait and a bank's repair demands.

A relative in another state can still sign, since the title company can set up remote signatures. For an empty house, the monthly drain of tax, utilities and insurance stops when the sale closes.

What to gather first

Before you call, pull the deed, the most recent tax notice, utility account details and any rental license paperwork. If the roof or cooling system is old, note roughly when it was installed. Buyers and title officers both ask for these items, and having them ready shortens the whole process.

Choices for Hurricane sellers

Three routes exist: hire an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. A listing demands showings while newer houses compete down the road. A cash buyer takes the property in present condition.

  • Empty houses still racking up tax, utility and insurance costs.
  • Short-term rentals that lost a license or fell short of city rules.
  • Inherited houses with heirs living out of state.
  • Older homes with tired roofs, evaporative coolers or failing air conditioning.

From any buyer, request a written closing date and proof of funds. Then set the number beside what a listing would bring home once repairs and commission come out.

Frequently asked questions

What is Hurricane's population?

The 2020 count was 20,036 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 25,745.

When is property tax due in Hurricane?

Every November 30, billed by the Washington County Treasurer, even if no notice arrives. There are no payment plans, but partial payments of $10 or more are accepted.

Does a short-term rental license transfer when I sell my Hurricane house?

No. The new owner has 45 days from purchase to apply for a fresh license, or the old one is forfeited. The buyer could then land on a waiting list.

Is Hurricane's climate hard on houses?

Yes, it can be. St. George, the nearest long-term station, averages a July high near 102 degrees with about 60 days a year at 100 or more, which wears on roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes.

Where is a deed recorded for a Hurricane house?

With the Washington County Recorder in St. George. Recordings are cut off at 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, and the title company usually files the deed for you.

Selling in West Haven?
We buy West Haven houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

West Haven at a glance

Roughly 35 miles north of Salt Lake City and west of the Wasatch range, West Haven is a city in Weber County. Neighbors are Ogden on the east, Roy on the south, Hooper on the west and Marriott-Slaterville on the north. Two rivers, the Weber and the Ogden, join in the northeast corner, around 4,269 feet up. Because the city belongs to the Ogden-Clearfield metro area, plenty of residents drive to jobs in Ogden, Roy and Davis County.

Population was 10,272 in 2010 and 16,739 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate at the top of this page is 25,627. A citywide sewer system arrived in 2002 and made denser building possible. West Haven became a city on July 1, 1991, when the old communities of Kanesville and Wilson combined, so farmhouses, older grid streets and new subdivisions all share one set of city limits. That is why two houses here can sell very differently.

Local figureValue
2020 census population16,739

Median household income$80,762
Weber County tax due dateNovember 30
Recording fee, first page$45.00

Homeowner vacancy was just 0.7% in 2020, so very few houses stand empty.

Four seasons and your house

Winters are cold and summers hot. Ogden, close by, sees an average July high of 91.3 degrees, a January low of 21.2 and about 16.4 inches of precipitation yearly, with a record low of minus 23 and a record high of 106. Snowfall typically starts around late October or early November and runs to April.

Those swings punish certain parts of a house:

  • Roofs and gutters holding snow and ice.
  • Exposed pipes and sprinkler lines that can freeze.
  • Furnaces, which run hard half the year.
  • Driveways and flatwork that crack through freeze and thaw cycles.

Inspectors check all of these, and an aging furnace often turns into a bargaining point.

Neighborhoods, trails and schools

By census definition the city is entirely urban, yet it still has a farm feel. Most neighborhoods are single-family, condominiums and multifamily buildings are being added, and some 19th-century farmhouses and working farms remain. The city bought 40 acres for a park in 1994, with playground equipment, sports fields and a historical marker. A River Parkway Trail is planned with a fishing bridge and a pedestrian tunnel under 21st Street, linking to the Weber County Centennial Trail.

A house close to the trails and schools draws families. One on a bigger rural lot draws people who want space for animals or outbuildings.

The Weber School District serves the city. Elementary schools in or near it are Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven, and junior high students attend Rocky Mountain or the newer Mountain View. Two of these buildings opened as recently as 2024, which shows how quickly families have arrived. Buyers with children often ask which school a house feeds, so confirm the boundary with the district before you advertise.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your West Haven house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Permits and city rules

West Haven's Community Development group handles the Building Department, business licensing, code enforcement and emergency management. The city offices are at 4150 S 3900 W, and the main line is 801-731-4519. Ask which permits apply before you begin repairs, and ask your title or escrow company what the buyer's lender will want to see.

A quick pre-listing checklist:

  • Finished basements, decks and sheds should have permits on file.
  • Open code complaints should be cleared with code enforcement.
  • Utility accounts, including the West Haven Special Service District bill, should be current.

Weber County property tax and recording

The county sends one property tax bill a year, payable by November 30. After that date the balance is delinquent on December 1 and penalties and interest are added. Expect valuation notices around July 20, tax notices in October, and an appeal deadline of September 15.

Utah takes 45% off the value of a primary residence, leaving 55% to tax. Weber County requires the home to be the occupant's main residence for at least 183 consecutive days in a year, and a renter's main home can qualify too. Nightly rentals, vacation homes and second homes cannot. When the county mails a declaration form, return it within 30 days or the exemption is dropped. The Assessor's line is (801) 399-8572 if you are unsure where you stand.

The Weber County Recorder takes deeds at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 370, in Ogden. The charge is $45.00 for the first page, none for further standard pages, and $2.00 per description beyond ten. At closing, the title company prorates property tax.

Your options for selling

Sellers here have three paths: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a cash offer. Which one fits depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you need to be done. Roof and furnace condition tend to set the price a buyer will offer.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Utah houses in their current shape. People who call us are often up against a deadline, such as a job change, an inherited property, a tenant situation, or a mortgage that has slipped behind. The process is simple: talk through the house, schedule a walk-through, receive a written offer, and pick the closing date. Bring the deed, the latest tax notice and any loan statement so the title company can confirm what is owed. Saying no costs you nothing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy West Haven houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Closing day and taxes owed

On closing day the title company pays off your mortgage, divides the year's property tax between you and the buyer, and files the new deed with the Weber County Recorder. Any unpaid tax is deducted from your proceeds, since the debt follows the parcel. A balance goes delinquent on December 1, and interest accrues on the previous year's balance from February 1. Paying it off before listing keeps the closing statement simple.

Request a payoff figure from the title company early, and ask who is covering the $45.00 first-page recording charge. Cash deals often close sooner because no lender is underwriting a loan, which lets you line the date up with a move.

What West Haven sellers often face

  • Competition from newly built houses in a city that has grown by tens of percent in a few years.
  • Older farmhouses and rural lots where the land and the house are valued differently.
  • Primary residence exemption questions when a house becomes a rental.
  • Out-of-state heirs who must sort out a deed and a recording before anything else.

If you inherited the house, the deed and recording come first, then the tax notice and any open balance. If you rented it out, confirm how the county currently treats the exemption before you close. Sellers who lived in the house for years sometimes forget they changed its use, and the Assessor can tell you what is on file for the parcel.

Frequently asked questions

What county is West Haven, UT in?

Weber County. Property tax, deeds and valuation appeals all go through Weber County offices in Ogden.

When is property tax due in West Haven?

The due date is November 30. A balance still open on December 1 is delinquent, and interest on the prior year's balance starts February 1.

What does it cost to record a deed in Weber County?

The Recorder charges $45.00 for the first page, nothing for additional standard pages, and $2.00 for each legal description over ten.

Which school district covers West Haven?

The Weber School District. Nearby elementary schools include Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven, with Rocky Mountain and Mountain View junior highs.

Can I sell a West Haven house as-is?

Yes. No rule makes you repair a house first. A buyer who purchases it in present condition lets you skip the repair bills.
